options.text: Configure AWS IAM Identity Center with AD Connector. Have developers use the AWS CLI with the aws configure sso command, which authenticates through the corporate IdP and provides temporary credentials that auto-refresh.
Create IAM users for each developer with programmatic access keys that are rotated every 90 days.
Set up a custom web application that authenticates developers against AD and uses STS AssumeRole to generate temporary credentials.
Share a single set of IAM credentials among the development team to minimize credential management.

explanation: IAM Identity Center with AD Connector integrates with the corporate Active Directory. The AWS CLI SSO feature authenticates developers through the corporate IdP and automatically manages temporary credentials that expire and refresh. No long-lived keys are created. Option B creates long-lived access keys, which the company wants to avoid. Option C requires building a custom application. Option D (shared credentials) violates security best practices and prevents individual accountability.

stem: A company is designing a solution to aggregate data from 50 different third-party SaaS applications into a central data warehouse. Each SaaS application has a different API (REST, GraphQL, or webhook-based). The company wants to minimize custom integration code. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon AppFlow to create flows from supported SaaS sources (Salesforce, Zendesk, ServiceNow, etc.) to Amazon S3 or Amazon Redshift. For unsupported sources, use AppFlow custom connectors built with Lambda.
Write custom Lambda functions for each of the 50 SaaS APIs and schedule them with EventBridge to pull data into S3.
Use AWS Glue crawlers to discover and import data from all 50 SaaS APIs automatically.
Deploy Apache NiFi on Amazon EMR to create data flows from all SaaS sources.

explanation: Amazon AppFlow provides pre-built connectors for many popular SaaS applications, eliminating custom integration code for supported sources. For unsupported sources, custom connectors can be built with Lambda. AppFlow handles authentication, data mapping, scheduling, and error handling. Option B requires writing and maintaining 50 custom integrations. Option C (Glue crawlers) cannot crawl SaaS APIs; they work with databases and file systems. Option D (NiFi on EMR) requires managing infrastructure and building custom processors.

stem: A company has a fleet of 500 EC2 instances across multiple accounts. The operations team needs to run shell commands on specific subsets of instances (e.g., all web servers in production, all database servers in staging) without using SSH keys. Which approach provides secure, auditable remote management?

options.text: Use AWS Systems Manager Run Command with resource groups based on instance tags. Configure Systems Manager Session Manager for interactive sessions. All commands are logged to CloudTrail and optionally to S3 and CloudWatch Logs.
Deploy a bastion host in each account and manage SSH keys for all 500 instances.
Use AWS Lambda to SSH into instances and execute commands remotely.
Install Ansible on a management server and use SSH-based playbooks to manage all instances.

explanation: Systems Manager Run Command executes commands on instances without SSH access, using the SSM agent and IAM authentication. Resource groups with tag-based targeting enable running commands on specific subsets (e.g., tag:Role=WebServer AND tag:Environment=Production). Session Manager provides interactive shell access. All activity is logged to CloudTrail. Option B (bastion hosts) requires SSH key management across 500 instances. Option C (Lambda SSH) requires key management and network access. Option D (Ansible) requires SSH access and key management.

stem: A company is modernizing its scheduling system that triggers batch jobs based on complex time-based rules (e.g., 'run every weekday at 2 AM EST except holidays, with a 30-minute retry window if the job fails'). The current system uses a cron daemon on a dedicated Linux server. Which AWS solution replaces this with the least operational overhead?

options.text: Use Amazon EventBridge Scheduler with cron and rate expressions to trigger AWS Step Functions workflows. Configure Step Functions retry policies with a 30-minute window. Maintain a holiday calendar in DynamoDB that the Step Functions workflow checks before proceeding.
Deploy a cron daemon on an EC2 instance and migrate the existing crontab configuration.
Use AWS Batch with scheduling enabled to run jobs on a fixed schedule.
Use CloudWatch Events with cron expressions to trigger Lambda functions directly.

explanation: EventBridge Scheduler supports cron expressions for time-based scheduling with timezone support. Step Functions provides workflow orchestration with built-in retry policies. DynamoDB stores the holiday calendar that the workflow checks to skip holiday executions. This is fully serverless with no infrastructure to manage. Option B (EC2 cron) is a lift-and-shift that does not reduce operational overhead. Option C (Batch) scheduling is more limited for complex rules. Option D (CloudWatch Events) has been superseded by EventBridge and does not provide workflow orchestration with retry policies.

stem: A company has an AWS Organization and wants to implement a consistent VPC architecture across all accounts. Every VPC must use specific CIDR blocks assigned from a central pool, and VPCs must not use overlapping CIDR ranges. How should the solutions architect manage CIDR allocation?

options.text: Use Amazon VPC IP Address Manager (IPAM) to create IP address pools and allocate CIDR blocks to accounts. Configure IPAM to enforce non-overlapping allocations and integrate with AWS Organizations for cross-account management.
Maintain a spreadsheet of CIDR allocations and have account administrators manually assign CIDRs when creating VPCs.
Use a fixed CIDR block for all VPCs since each VPC is isolated by default.
Use AWS CloudFormation with a custom resource that queries a DynamoDB table for available CIDR blocks before creating VPCs.

explanation: VPC IPAM provides centralized IP address management with automated CIDR allocation from defined pools. It enforces non-overlapping CIDR assignments across accounts, integrates with AWS Organizations for cross-account governance, and tracks IP usage. This is the AWS-native solution for IP address management. Option B (spreadsheet) is error-prone and does not scale. Option C (fixed CIDR) causes overlaps that prevent VPC peering and Transit Gateway connectivity. Option D (custom solution) works but adds maintenance overhead compared to the native IPAM service.

stem: A company is building an API backend that serves product recommendations. The recommendations are generated by a batch ML model that runs daily and produces a set of recommendations for each user. The API must serve these pre-computed recommendations with sub-10ms latency to 1 million daily active users. Which architecture provides this performance?

options.text: Store pre-computed recommendations in Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with each user's recommendations as a Redis hash. Serve the API through API Gateway backed by Lambda that reads from ElastiCache.
Store recommendations in Amazon S3 as JSON files and serve through CloudFront with S3 as the origin.
Store recommendations in Amazon RDS and implement application-level caching in the API layer.
Use Amazon SageMaker real-time inference to generate recommendations on each API call.

explanation: ElastiCache for Redis provides sub-millisecond read latency, easily meeting the sub-10ms requirement. Redis hashes efficiently store per-user recommendation sets. Lambda reads from ElastiCache with VPC access. For 1 million DAU, the dataset fits comfortably in Redis memory. Option B (S3/CloudFront) has higher latency than ElastiCache for individual key lookups. Option C (RDS) provides single-digit millisecond latency, which is close but adding application caching adds complexity. Option D (SageMaker inference) generates on the fly, which is unnecessary since recommendations are pre-computed and adds latency.

stem: A company has an existing application that writes data to Amazon DynamoDB. The application needs to maintain a materialized view of the data in Amazon OpenSearch Service for full-text search capabilities. Currently, the application performs dual writes to both DynamoDB and OpenSearch, but the operations team reports data inconsistencies between the two stores. How should the solutions architect fix this?

options.text: Replace the dual-write pattern with DynamoDB Streams. Configure a Lambda function to process the stream and update OpenSearch. This ensures that every change in DynamoDB is reliably propagated to OpenSearch.
Increase the application's retry logic for OpenSearch writes to reduce inconsistencies.
Schedule a periodic full sync job that copies all DynamoDB data to OpenSearch every hour.
Replace DynamoDB with OpenSearch as the primary data store to eliminate synchronization.

explanation: DynamoDB Streams captures every change (insert, update, delete) as an ordered stream of events. Lambda processes these events and updates OpenSearch, ensuring eventual consistency. This is more reliable than dual writes because DynamoDB Streams guarantees delivery. If the Lambda function fails, it retries automatically. Option B (retry logic) reduces but does not eliminate inconsistencies from partial failures. Option C (periodic sync) creates hourly stale data windows. Option D (OpenSearch only) loses DynamoDB's transactional capabilities and key-value performance.

stem: A company is modernizing its ETL pipeline from on-premises Informatica to AWS. The pipeline involves extracting data from 20 relational databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server), transforming the data with complex business rules, and loading it into a data warehouse. Which AWS-native solution replaces Informatica with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Use AWS Glue Studio for visual ETL job creation with built-in connectors for all four database engines. Use AWS Glue Data Catalog for metadata management and AWS Glue workflows for orchestration.
Use Amazon EMR with Apache Spark and write custom PySpark scripts for all ETL transformations.
Deploy Apache Airflow on Amazon MWAA for orchestration with custom Python ETL scripts running on EC2.
Use AWS Data Pipeline to orchestrate data movement between the databases and the data warehouse.

explanation: AWS Glue Studio provides a visual interface for creating ETL jobs, similar to Informatica's visual paradigm. Built-in JDBC connectors support MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, and SQL Server. The Data Catalog serves as a central metadata repository. Glue workflows orchestrate the pipeline. This is fully serverless with no infrastructure management. Option B (EMR/Spark) requires managing clusters and writing custom code. Option C (MWAA/EC2) requires managing infrastructure. Option D (Data Pipeline) is being deprecated in favor of Glue and Step Functions.

stem: A company has a complex CI/CD pipeline that deploys to multiple AWS accounts. The pipeline uses AWS CodePipeline in a tooling account. Deployments to the staging account should be automatic, but deployments to production must require approval from two different team members. Which configuration achieves this?

options.text: Configure the CodePipeline with a manual approval action before the production deploy stage. Configure the approval action to require two approvals using SNS notifications to the approver group. Use cross-account IAM roles for deployments.
Create two separate CodePipelines: one for staging (automatic) and one for production (with approval).
Use CodePipeline with a Lambda function that checks for two approved entries in a DynamoDB table before proceeding.
Configure CodePipeline with an IAM policy that requires two different IAM users to approve the production stage.

explanation: CodePipeline's manual approval action supports requiring multiple approvals (configurable) before proceeding. SNS notifications alert approvers. The staging deploy stage runs automatically, and the production deploy stage is preceded by the approval action. Cross-account IAM roles enable deployments to different accounts from the tooling account pipeline. Option B (separate pipelines) loses the single pipeline visibility and code promotion workflow. Option C (custom Lambda/DynamoDB) adds unnecessary complexity. Option D (IAM policy for approval) is not how CodePipeline approval works.

stem: A company is building a highly available message processing system. Messages must be processed exactly once and in the exact order they were received. The system must handle 1,000 messages per second and each message must be processed within 30 seconds. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon SQS FIFO queue with message deduplication enabled and a message group ID strategy that preserves ordering. Process messages with a fleet of consumers using the ReceiveMessage API with a visibility timeout of 30 seconds.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with a single shard for strict ordering and Lambda for processing.
Use Amazon SQS Standard queue with application-level deduplication and ordering logic.
Use Amazon MQ with ActiveMQ for exactly-once delivery with message ordering.

explanation: SQS FIFO queues guarantee exactly-once processing and strict ordering within message groups. High-throughput FIFO queues support up to 70,000 messages per second with batching. Message deduplication prevents duplicate processing. The visibility timeout ensures messages are not reprocessed while being handled. Option B (Kinesis single shard) is limited to 1,000 records per second per shard for writes, but Kinesis provides at-least-once delivery, not exactly-once. Option C (Standard SQS) does not guarantee ordering or exactly-once delivery. Option D (ActiveMQ) requires managing the broker infrastructure.

stem: A company has a data lake in Amazon S3 with petabytes of data in Parquet format. Analysts use Amazon Athena for ad-hoc queries but report that queries on large tables take over 10 minutes. The tables have hundreds of partitions organized by date. What optimizations should the solutions architect implement to improve Athena query performance?

options.text: Optimize Parquet files to have a target size of 128-512 MB each, use partition projection in Athena to eliminate partition discovery overhead, and add predicate pushdown filters using bloom filters in the Parquet files.
Convert all data from Parquet to CSV format for faster Athena scanning.
Move all data to Amazon Redshift for better query performance.
Increase the number of partitions by adding more granular partition keys (hour, minute) to all tables.

explanation: Optimizing Parquet file sizes to 128-512 MB reduces the overhead of opening many small files. Partition projection eliminates the need to crawl the Glue Data Catalog for partition metadata, reducing query planning time. Predicate pushdown with bloom filters allows Athena to skip Parquet row groups that do not contain matching data. Option B (CSV) is significantly less efficient than Parquet for analytical queries. Option C (Redshift) requires data loading and adds cost. Option D (more partitions) can worsen performance with too many small files per partition.

stem: A company is decomposing a monolithic application into microservices on AWS. The team needs a service mesh to manage service-to-service communication, implement traffic routing, and provide observability across services running on Amazon ECS Fargate. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Deploy AWS App Mesh with Envoy proxies as sidecar containers in each ECS task. Configure virtual services and virtual routers for traffic management and enable App Mesh integration with AWS X-Ray for observability.
Use Application Load Balancers between each service pair for traffic routing and implement custom logging for observability.
Deploy Istio on Amazon EKS and migrate all services from ECS to EKS for service mesh capabilities.
Implement service discovery using AWS Cloud Map and handle traffic routing in application code.

explanation: AWS App Mesh provides a managed service mesh for ECS Fargate with Envoy proxies as sidecars. It handles traffic routing (canary, weighted, header-based), retry policies, circuit breaking, and provides observability through X-Ray integration. This works natively with ECS Fargate. Option B (ALBs per service pair) creates many ALBs and lacks advanced traffic management. Option C (Istio/EKS) requires migrating from ECS to EKS. Option D (Cloud Map) provides service discovery but not traffic management or observability.

stem: A company needs to securely transfer sensitive data between its on-premises environment and an Amazon S3 bucket. The data must be encrypted in transit using a private connection, and the traffic must not traverse the public internet. The company already has an AWS Direct Connect connection. Which solution ensures the data never crosses the public internet?

options.text: Create a VPC with a VPC endpoint for S3 (gateway endpoint). Establish a private VIF on the Direct Connect connection to the VPC. Route S3 traffic from on-premises through the Direct Connect private VIF to the VPC, then through the S3 gateway endpoint.
Use a Direct Connect public VIF to access S3 directly over the Direct Connect connection.
Use AWS Site-to-Site VPN over the Direct Connect connection to encrypt traffic and access S3 through the VPN tunnel.
Transfer the data to an EC2 instance in the VPC first via Direct Connect, then copy from EC2 to S3.

explanation: This architecture keeps all traffic on private paths. The Direct Connect private VIF connects on-premises to the VPC. The S3 gateway endpoint routes S3 traffic within the AWS network, never touching the public internet. Data is encrypted in transit using HTTPS. Option B (public VIF) technically uses AWS backbone but the public VIF addresses are public. Option C (VPN) adds encryption but does not change the routing path for S3 access. Option D adds an unnecessary intermediate step through EC2.

stem: A company is designing a system that must maintain a highly consistent, durable configuration store for a distributed application. The configuration must support atomic updates, versioning, and the ability to roll back to previous versions. Updates occur less than once per minute but reads happen thousands of times per second. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use AWS AppConfig with a configuration profile stored in Systems Manager Parameter Store. AppConfig provides built-in validation, gradual deployment, and automatic rollback for configuration changes.
Store configuration in an Amazon DynamoDB table with strongly consistent reads and enable DynamoDB Streams for change notification.
Store configuration in an S3 bucket with versioning enabled and use CloudFront for caching reads.
Use AWS Secrets Manager for all configuration values with rotation enabled.

explanation: AWS AppConfig provides feature flags and application configuration with built-in validation, gradual deployment strategies (rolling, all-at-once), and automatic rollback if a deployment causes errors. Parameter Store provides versioning and history. AppConfig caches configurations locally in the application, handling thousands of reads per second without external calls. Option B (DynamoDB) works but requires building deployment and rollback logic. Option C (S3) lacks atomic updates and deployment strategies. Option D (Secrets Manager) is for secrets, not general configuration, and is expensive for high-read scenarios.

stem: A company is running a data processing pipeline on Amazon EMR that processes 5 TB of data daily. The EMR cluster runs 24/7 but is only actively processing data for 8 hours per day. The rest of the time, the cluster is idle. How should the solutions architect optimize costs?

options.text: Convert to transient EMR clusters that are launched by AWS Step Functions when processing is needed, use Spot Instances for task nodes, and terminate the cluster after processing completes. Store intermediate data in S3.
Purchase Reserved Instances for the EMR cluster to reduce the hourly cost.
Reduce the cluster size to the minimum and scale up during processing hours using EMR managed scaling.
Migrate from EMR to AWS Glue for serverless processing that charges only for compute time used.

explanation: Transient clusters run only during the 8-hour processing window, eliminating 16 hours of idle compute costs (67% savings). Step Functions orchestrates the cluster lifecycle (create, submit jobs, terminate). Spot Instances for task nodes provide additional savings (up to 90%). S3 decouples storage from compute, ensuring data persists between cluster runs. Option B (Reserved Instances) still wastes money during idle hours. Option C (managed scaling) reduces but does not eliminate idle costs. Option D (Glue) may work but could require rewriting complex EMR/Spark jobs.

stem: A company is migrating from a commercially licensed relational database (Oracle) to an open-source database on AWS. The application uses Oracle-specific features including materialized views, database links, and Oracle Advanced Queuing. The company wants to minimize licensing costs while maintaining feature compatibility. Which target database should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition. Use AWS SCT to identify Oracle features that have PostgreSQL equivalents (materialized views are natively supported), and use SCT's migration assessment report to plan manual conversion for features without direct equivalents.
Amazon Aurora MySQL-Compatible Edition because MySQL is the most widely used open-source database.
Amazon RDS for MariaDB because it was forked from MySQL with additional enterprise features.
Amazon DynamoDB to completely eliminate relational database licensing.

explanation: PostgreSQL has the highest feature compatibility with Oracle among open-source databases. It natively supports materialized views, has extensions for database links (dblink, postgres_fdw), and provides pub/sub capabilities similar to Oracle AQ. AWS SCT provides the most comprehensive migration path from Oracle to PostgreSQL. Option B (MySQL) has lower feature compatibility with Oracle than PostgreSQL. Option C (MariaDB) also has lower compatibility. Option D (DynamoDB) requires a complete rewrite from relational to NoSQL.

stem: A company is implementing a data classification and protection strategy for its AWS environment. The company needs to automatically discover and classify sensitive data (PII, financial data, healthcare records) across hundreds of S3 buckets in multiple accounts and take automated action when sensitive data is found in non-compliant locations. Which TWO services should the solutions architect configure? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Use Amazon Macie to automatically discover and classify sensitive data across S3 buckets in the organization.
Configure Amazon EventBridge rules to trigger AWS Lambda functions when Macie findings indicate sensitive data in non-compliant buckets, automatically moving or encrypting the data.
Use AWS Glue DataBrew to profile and classify data in S3 buckets.
Deploy custom regex-based scanning scripts on EC2 instances to classify S3 data.
Use Amazon Rekognition to identify sensitive content in images stored in S3.

explanation: Macie (A) uses machine learning to automatically discover and classify sensitive data (PII, financial data, healthcare records) across S3 buckets. It integrates with AWS Organizations for multi-account scanning. EventBridge with Lambda (B) enables automated response to Macie findings, such as moving sensitive data to compliant buckets or applying encryption. Option C (Glue DataBrew) is for data profiling and transformation, not security classification. Option D (custom scripts) does not scale and lacks ML-based classification. Option E (Rekognition) is for image/video analysis, not data classification.

stem: A company is building an application that needs to serve responses to users within 5 ms from any location globally. The data is 10 GB of key-value pairs that are updated hourly. Which solution achieves this latency requirement?

options.text: Use Amazon CloudFront with Lambda@Edge functions that read from a DynamoDB Global Table in the nearest Region.
Deploy Amazon ElastiCache for Redis Global Datastore with nodes in multiple Regions and use AWS Global Accelerator to route users to the nearest node.
Use Amazon CloudFront with S3 as the origin, caching key-value responses at edge locations with appropriate cache TTLs matching the hourly update cycle.
Deploy the application in a single Region and use Route 53 latency-based routing.

explanation: CloudFront caches responses at 400+ edge locations globally, providing sub-5ms latency for cached content. Since data updates hourly, setting a 1-hour cache TTL matches the update cycle. S3 stores the key-value data as individual objects or a manifest file. CloudFront serves cached responses in microseconds. Option A (Lambda@Edge + DynamoDB) adds Lambda execution time and DynamoDB query latency, exceeding 5ms. Option B (ElastiCache Global Datastore) provides sub-millisecond in-Region but cross-Region adds network latency. Option D (single Region) cannot achieve 5ms globally.

stem: A company has an application that uses Amazon SQS Standard queues for asynchronous message processing. Messages are occasionally processed more than once, causing duplicate records in the database. The application team cannot modify the consumer code to add idempotency checks. How should the solutions architect solve this with minimal application changes?

options.text: Migrate from SQS Standard to SQS FIFO queue with content-based deduplication enabled. Update only the queue URL in the application configuration.
Add a DynamoDB table to track processed message IDs and check it before processing each message.
Increase the SQS visibility timeout to prevent redelivery of messages.
Configure the SQS queue to delete messages immediately after delivery to prevent redelivery.

explanation: SQS FIFO queues with content-based deduplication automatically prevent duplicate messages within a 5-minute deduplication window. The only application change needed is updating the queue URL to the FIFO queue endpoint. Content-based deduplication uses a SHA-256 hash of the message body to detect duplicates. Option B requires application code changes, which the team cannot make. Option C (longer visibility timeout) does not prevent duplicates from infrastructure failures. Option D (immediate deletion) risks message loss if processing fails.

stem: A company is migrating to a multi-account AWS environment. The company needs to decide on an OU structure for AWS Organizations. The company has teams organized by business unit (Retail, Healthcare, Finance) and by function (Development, Staging, Production). Which OU structure provides the most effective governance?

options.text: Create top-level OUs for each environment (Development, Staging, Production) with nested OUs for business units under each environment. Apply environment-specific SCPs at the top level and business-unit-specific SCPs at the nested level.
Create a flat structure with all accounts in a single OU and manage everything through IAM policies.
Create top-level OUs for each business unit with all environments (Dev/Staging/Prod) mixed in each business unit OU.
Create separate AWS Organizations for each business unit, each with its own OU hierarchy.

explanation: Environment-based top-level OUs (Production, Staging, Development) allow applying different security governance per environment. For example, Production gets the most restrictive SCPs (no direct console access, mandatory encryption), while Development gets more permissive policies. Business-unit nested OUs allow additional team-specific controls. This is the AWS recommended OU structure. Option B (flat structure) loses the ability to apply different policies per environment. Option C (business unit top-level) makes it harder to enforce consistent environment-specific controls. Option D (separate organizations) loses consolidated billing and centralized governance.

stem: A company needs to build a backend API that handles file uploads up to 5 GB. The uploads must be resumable (if a network interruption occurs, the upload can continue from where it left off). The API must support 10,000 concurrent uploads. Which architecture supports this?

options.text: Generate S3 presigned URLs for multipart upload from the API backend. The client uses the presigned URLs to upload parts directly to S3, enabling parallel uploads and resumability. The API backend initiates and completes the multipart upload.
Accept file uploads through Amazon API Gateway and proxy them to Lambda for storage in S3.
Use AWS Transfer Family with SFTP protocol for all file uploads.
Deploy an NGINX reverse proxy on EC2 to receive uploads and forward them to S3.

explanation: S3 multipart upload with presigned URLs allows clients to upload file parts directly to S3, bypassing the API servers. Each part is independently uploaded, so if a network interruption occurs, only the interrupted part needs to be re-uploaded (resumability). Presigned URLs handle authorization without exposing credentials. S3 natively handles 10,000 concurrent uploads. Option B (API Gateway/Lambda) has a 10 MB payload limit. Option C (SFTP) does not provide a REST API interface. Option D (NGINX) creates a bottleneck and single point of failure.

stem: A company has a VPC with public and private subnets. The NAT Gateway costs are unexpectedly high at $5,000/month. Analysis shows that the majority of NAT Gateway traffic is from EC2 instances in private subnets accessing AWS services (S3, DynamoDB, STS, CloudWatch). How should the solutions architect reduce NAT Gateway costs?

options.text: Create VPC gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB, and VPC interface endpoints for STS and CloudWatch. Update route tables and security groups to direct AWS service traffic through the endpoints instead of the NAT Gateway.
Move all EC2 instances to public subnets with Elastic IP addresses to eliminate NAT Gateway usage.
Replace the NAT Gateway with a NAT instance on a t3.micro for lower cost.
Reduce the number of API calls to AWS services from the EC2 instances.

explanation: VPC gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB are free and route traffic within the AWS network. Interface endpoints for STS and CloudWatch cost less than NAT Gateway data processing charges. By directing AWS service traffic through endpoints, the bulk of NAT Gateway traffic is eliminated. Option B (public subnets) exposes instances to the internet, creating security risks. Option C (NAT instance) is less reliable and has bandwidth limitations. Option D (reduce API calls) may not be feasible without application changes.

stem: A company has a legacy application that uses LDAP for user directory services. The LDAP server runs on-premises and is integrated with 30 applications. The company wants to migrate the LDAP directory to AWS while maintaining LDAP compatibility for existing applications. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Deploy AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory (AWS Managed Microsoft AD), which supports LDAP protocol. Migrate the existing LDAP directory data to AWS Managed Microsoft AD.
Migrate to Amazon Cognito user pools and update all 30 applications to use the Cognito SDK.
Deploy OpenLDAP on Amazon EC2 instances and manually manage the LDAP server.
Use AWS IAM Identity Center as a replacement for the LDAP directory.

explanation: AWS Managed Microsoft AD supports the LDAP protocol natively, maintaining compatibility with existing applications that use LDAP queries. It is fully managed by AWS (patching, backups, replication). Directory data can be migrated using standard LDAP tools. Option B (Cognito) requires rewriting all 30 applications. Option C (EC2 OpenLDAP) requires managing the LDAP server. Option D (IAM Identity Center) is for AWS account access, not a general-purpose LDAP directory.

stem: A company needs to implement a solution that ensures all Amazon EBS volumes are encrypted by default in all accounts across the organization. The solution must also prevent users from launching instances with unencrypted EBS volumes. Which approach provides the strongest enforcement?

options.text: Use CloudFormation StackSets to enable the EBS encryption by default setting in all accounts and Regions. Create an SCP that denies ec2:RunInstances and ec2:CreateVolume when the ec2:Encrypted condition is false.
Enable EBS encryption by default in the management account and it will automatically propagate to all member accounts.
Create an AWS Config rule that detects unencrypted EBS volumes and use auto-remediation to encrypt them.
Add IAM policies to all roles that deny creating unencrypted EBS volumes.

explanation: CloudFormation StackSets deploy the EBS encryption by default setting across all accounts and Regions consistently. The SCP provides a preventive guardrail that cannot be bypassed by account administrators, denying any attempt to create unencrypted volumes. This two-layer approach ensures both default behavior and enforcement. Option B is incorrect because EBS encryption settings do not propagate from the management account. Option C is reactive, not preventive. Option D (IAM policies) can be modified by account administrators.

stem: A company is building an event-driven architecture where business events (order placed, payment received, shipment dispatched) are generated by multiple producer services. Multiple consumer services need to subscribe to different combinations of events. The company needs an event bus that supports content-based filtering, event replay, and schema validation. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon EventBridge with a custom event bus. Define EventBridge rules with content-based event patterns for routing. Use EventBridge Schema Registry for schema validation and EventBridge Archive for event replay.
Use Amazon SNS with message filtering policies and SQS queues for each consumer.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with consumer-side filtering in Lambda functions.
Deploy Apache Kafka on Amazon MSK with consumer groups for event subscription.

explanation: EventBridge provides content-based filtering through event rules with JSON patterns, schema validation through the Schema Registry, and event replay through Archive and Replay features. The custom event bus isolates business events from AWS service events. Option B (SNS/SQS) supports filtering but lacks schema validation and event replay. Option C (Kinesis) requires consumer-side filtering and lacks schema validation. Option D (MSK) requires managing infrastructure and does not have built-in content-based routing.

stem: A company has a global application using Amazon Route 53 with weighted routing to distribute traffic 70/30 between us-east-1 and eu-west-1. The company wants to perform a canary deployment of a new version in us-east-1, sending only 5% of that Region's traffic to the new version while monitoring for errors. Which approach should the solutions architect use?

options.text: In us-east-1, deploy the new version to a separate target group on the ALB. Configure the ALB listener rules with weighted target groups, sending 5% of traffic to the new target group and 95% to the existing target group.
Change the Route 53 weighted routing to send 5% to the new version's endpoint and 95% to the existing endpoint.
Use CloudFront with Lambda@Edge to randomly route 5% of requests to the new version based on a random number.
Deploy the new version to 5% of EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group using a rolling update.

explanation: ALB weighted target groups provide precise traffic splitting at the application layer within the Region. This keeps the Route 53 70/30 Regional routing intact while implementing the 5% canary within us-east-1. Traffic shifting can be monitored and adjusted in real-time. Option B (Route 53) would change the global traffic distribution, not the per-Region canary. Option C (Lambda@Edge) adds complexity for a simple traffic split. Option D (rolling update on 5% of instances) does not provide a clean rollback path since some instances have the new version.

stem: A company is modernizing its on-premises ETL pipeline that currently uses Apache Spark running on a Hadoop cluster. The pipeline processes 2 TB of data daily and the team is experienced with PySpark. The company wants to keep using Spark on AWS with minimal code changes and reduced operational overhead. Which service should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use AWS Glue with PySpark scripts. Glue provides a serverless Apache Spark environment that runs existing PySpark code with minimal modifications. Glue handles cluster provisioning, scaling, and management.
Deploy Apache Spark on Amazon EMR with managed scaling for automatic cluster resizing.
Rewrite the PySpark code as AWS Lambda functions for serverless execution.
Deploy Apache Spark on Amazon EKS using the Spark Kubernetes operator.

explanation: AWS Glue runs Apache Spark natively and accepts PySpark scripts with minimal modifications. It is fully serverless, automatically provisioning and scaling Spark workers based on the data volume. The team's existing PySpark expertise transfers directly. Option B (EMR) is valid but requires managing cluster lifecycle and configuration. Option C (Lambda) requires a complete rewrite from Spark. Option D (EKS Spark) adds Kubernetes management overhead.

stem: A company operates in a heavily regulated industry and must demonstrate to auditors that specific AWS resources have not been modified outside of approved change management processes. The auditors need historical evidence of resource configurations at any point in time for the past 2 years. Which AWS service provides this capability?

options.text: Use AWS Config with configuration recording enabled for all resource types. Configure a delivery channel to store configuration history in S3. Use Config timeline to view historical resource configurations at any point in time.
Use AWS CloudTrail to track all API calls and reconstruct resource configurations from the API call history.
Use AWS Systems Manager Inventory to track resource configurations over time.
Take daily snapshots of all resources and store them in S3 with lifecycle policies for 2-year retention.

explanation: AWS Config records configuration changes for supported resources, storing a complete history with timestamps. The configuration timeline shows the exact state of any resource at any point in time. Configuration snapshots in S3 provide durable historical records. This is purpose-built for compliance and audit requirements. Option B (CloudTrail) logs API calls but does not directly show resource configurations. Option C (Systems Manager Inventory) tracks EC2 instance software, not all resource configurations. Option D (snapshots) is manual and does not cover all resource types.

stem: A company is building a search engine for an e-commerce platform with 50 million products. The search must support full-text search, faceted navigation (filter by category, price range, brand), autocomplete suggestions, and relevance scoring. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon OpenSearch Service with dedicated master nodes and data nodes. Configure index mappings for product fields, implement faceted search using aggregations, and use the suggest API for autocomplete.
Use Amazon DynamoDB with Global Secondary Indexes for search and filtering.
Use Amazon RDS with full-text search indexes and LIKE queries for search functionality.
Use Amazon CloudSearch for the product search engine.

explanation: OpenSearch (Elasticsearch) provides full-text search with relevance scoring (BM25), aggregations for faceted navigation, suggesters for autocomplete, and handles 50 million documents efficiently. Dedicated master nodes ensure cluster stability under load. Option B (DynamoDB) does not support full-text search or faceted navigation. Option C (RDS full-text) does not scale to 50 million products or support faceted search efficiently. Option D (CloudSearch) is a valid option but has fewer features and less community support than OpenSearch.

stem: A company has an application that processes messages from an Amazon SQS queue. The processing Lambda function occasionally encounters messages that cause it to fail repeatedly. After the maximum retry count, these 'poison pill' messages block processing of subsequent messages in the queue. How should the solutions architect handle this?

options.text: Configure a dead-letter queue (DLQ) on the SQS source queue with a maxReceiveCount of 3. Failed messages are automatically moved to the DLQ after 3 attempts, allowing the main queue to continue processing. Set up a CloudWatch alarm on the DLQ message count for monitoring.
Increase the Lambda function timeout to give more time for processing difficult messages.
Increase the SQS visibility timeout to prevent redelivery of failed messages.
Delete messages from the queue immediately after receipt, before processing.

explanation: A dead-letter queue isolates poison pill messages after a specified number of processing attempts (maxReceiveCount). This prevents problematic messages from blocking the main queue. The CloudWatch alarm alerts the team to investigate failed messages. The DLQ preserves the messages for analysis and potential reprocessing. Option B (longer timeout) does not help if the message is fundamentally unprocessable. Option C (longer visibility timeout) delays retries but does not prevent repeated failures. Option D (immediate deletion) risks data loss.

stem: A company is migrating its CI/CD pipeline from Jenkins running on-premises to AWS. The pipeline builds Java and Node.js applications, runs unit tests, deploys to staging, runs integration tests, and deploys to production with manual approval. Which AWS-native CI/CD solution should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use AWS CodeCommit for source control, AWS CodeBuild for building and testing (with separate build projects for Java and Node.js), AWS CodePipeline for orchestration including manual approval actions, and AWS CodeDeploy for deployments.
Deploy Jenkins on Amazon ECS Fargate for the same pipeline functionality on AWS infrastructure.
Use GitHub Actions with AWS integrations for the CI/CD pipeline.
Use AWS Amplify CI/CD for all application builds and deployments.

explanation: The AWS CodeSuite provides a complete CI/CD pipeline: CodeCommit for Git source control, CodeBuild for building and testing (supporting multiple languages), CodePipeline for orchestration with manual approval gates, and CodeDeploy for controlled deployments. This is fully managed with no infrastructure to maintain. Option B (Jenkins on Fargate) still requires managing Jenkins. Option C (GitHub Actions) is not AWS-native and has less integration with AWS deployment services. Option D (Amplify) is primarily for frontend and serverless applications.

stem: A company needs to provide its data science team with access to sensitive datasets while preventing data exfiltration. Data scientists must be able to run Jupyter notebooks, train ML models, and visualize results, but they should not be able to download data to their local machines or copy data outside the approved environment. Which solution should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Use Amazon SageMaker Studio with VPC-only mode (no internet access). Configure VPC endpoints for required services. Use SCP to deny S3 actions to non-approved buckets. Disable clipboard and file download in SageMaker Studio.
Set up Amazon WorkSpaces virtual desktops with Jupyter Notebook installed and restrict USB and clipboard functionality.
Create EC2 instances with Jupyter Notebook installed in a private subnet and grant data scientists SSH access.
Use Amazon EMR Notebooks with network restrictions to limit external access.

explanation: SageMaker Studio in VPC-only mode provides a managed Jupyter environment without internet access, preventing data exfiltration. VPC endpoints enable access to approved AWS services only. SCPs restrict S3 access to approved buckets. Disabling clipboard and file download prevents copying data to local machines. This provides a secure data science environment. Option B (WorkSpaces) requires manual Jupyter setup and lacks SageMaker's ML features. Option C (EC2 SSH) provides too much access and lacks data exfiltration controls. Option D (EMR Notebooks) requires managing EMR clusters.

stem: A company is building a ticket reservation system for a concert venue. The system must handle flash sales where 50,000 users simultaneously attempt to purchase tickets. The system must prevent overselling (no more tickets sold than available) and handle the burst traffic without errors. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon API Gateway with throttling, Amazon SQS to queue purchase requests, and a Lambda function that uses DynamoDB conditional writes (atomic decrement of available ticket count) to ensure no overselling.
Use an Application Load Balancer with an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances connected to Amazon RDS with row-level locking for ticket inventory.
Use Amazon CloudFront to cache the ticket purchase page and backend on a single large EC2 instance.
Use AWS Step Functions to orchestrate each ticket purchase as a workflow with Amazon Aurora as the backend.

explanation: SQS absorbs the burst of 50,000 concurrent requests, smoothing the load on the backend. Lambda processes requests from the queue. DynamoDB conditional writes (decrement available count only if count > 0) provide atomic operations that prevent overselling without complex locking. API Gateway throttling protects the system from overload. Option B (RDS with locking) creates database contention under high concurrency. Option C (single EC2) is a single point of failure and cannot handle the burst. Option D (Step Functions per purchase) adds unnecessary latency for each transaction.

stem: A company runs an Amazon EKS cluster that hosts 100 microservices. The cluster uses Amazon EBS gp3 volumes for persistent storage. The company has noticed that storage costs are high because many PersistentVolumeClaims (PVCs) have over-provisioned storage that is not fully utilized. How should the solutions architect optimize storage costs?

options.text: Implement the Amazon EBS CSI driver with volume resizing support. Monitor PVC utilization using CloudWatch Container Insights, identify over-provisioned volumes, and resize them downward. Use EBS Elastic Volumes for online resizing without downtime.
Replace all EBS volumes with Amazon EFS for shared storage to simplify capacity management.
Delete and recreate all PVCs with smaller sizes during a maintenance window.
Switch from EBS gp3 to EBS sc1 volumes for cost savings.

explanation: The EBS CSI driver supports volume expansion (though EBS does not natively support shrinking, you can create new smaller volumes and migrate data). CloudWatch Container Insights provides utilization metrics for identifying over-provisioned volumes. Elastic Volumes allow online resizing for volumes that need more space. The key optimization is identifying which volumes are over-provisioned. Option B (EFS) may increase costs for workloads that do not need shared storage. Option C is disruptive. Option D (sc1) is for sequential access patterns, not the random I/O typical of databases.

stem: A company is migrating a large Oracle database (10 TB) to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. The migration must have minimal downtime (under 4 hours). The database has complex schemas with thousands of stored procedures, triggers, and views. Which TWO steps are critical for this migration? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Use AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) to assess the migration complexity, convert the database schema, and identify stored procedures that require manual conversion.
Use AWS DMS with full-load and CDC (change data capture) to migrate the data with ongoing replication until cutover, minimizing downtime.
Use pg_dump to export the Oracle database and pg_restore to import into Aurora PostgreSQL.
Manually recreate all database objects in Aurora PostgreSQL by hand.
Use AWS Snowball to transfer the 10 TB of database data to Aurora PostgreSQL.

explanation: SCT (A) is essential for heterogeneous migrations (Oracle to PostgreSQL). It converts schemas, stored procedures, and views, and generates assessment reports identifying items requiring manual conversion. DMS with CDC (B) enables minimal downtime by replicating data continuously until cutover, which is critical for a 10 TB database. Option C (pg_dump) is a PostgreSQL tool that cannot export from Oracle. Option D (manual recreation) is extremely time-consuming for thousands of objects. Option E (Snowball) is for offline data transfer and cannot maintain ongoing replication.

stem: A company needs to implement a solution where Lambda functions in a workload account can access DynamoDB tables in a shared data account. The access must be controlled through IAM roles, and the workload account should not be able to escalate its own permissions. Which configuration achieves this?

options.text: Create an IAM role in the shared data account with a trust policy that allows the workload account's Lambda execution role to assume it. The role has a policy granting specific DynamoDB actions on specific tables. The Lambda function assumes this cross-account role for DynamoDB access.
Create a DynamoDB resource-based policy that grants access to the workload account.
Share the DynamoDB table using AWS RAM with the workload account.
Replicate the DynamoDB table to the workload account using DynamoDB Global Tables.

explanation: Cross-account IAM role assumption is the standard pattern for cross-account DynamoDB access. The trust policy in the data account controls which principals can assume the role. The permission policy on the role defines exactly which DynamoDB actions and tables are accessible. The workload account cannot modify the role in the data account. Option B is incorrect because DynamoDB does not support resource-based policies. Option C is incorrect because DynamoDB does not support AWS RAM sharing. Option D (Global Tables) replicates data, which is unnecessary for cross-account read/write access.

stem: A company is building a solution to process insurance claim documents. Each document is a multi-page PDF containing handwritten notes, printed forms, and attached photographs. The system must extract text from printed and handwritten content, identify key entities (names, dates, amounts), and classify the claim type. Which combination of services should the solutions architect use?

options.text: Use Amazon Textract to extract text from printed and handwritten content in PDFs, Amazon Comprehend to identify entities (names, dates, amounts), and Amazon Comprehend custom classifiers to classify the claim type.
Use Amazon Rekognition for text detection in images, Amazon Translate for text processing, and Amazon Lex for entity extraction.
Use a custom OCR model trained on Amazon SageMaker for text extraction and a Lambda function with regex patterns for entity extraction.
Use AWS Glue DataBrew to extract and profile data from PDF documents.

explanation: Textract is specifically designed for extracting text from documents, supporting both printed and handwritten content, tables, and forms in PDFs. Comprehend provides pre-built entity recognition for names, dates, and amounts. Custom Comprehend classifiers can be trained to classify claim types. Option B (Rekognition) is for image/video analysis, not document text extraction. Option C (custom OCR) requires building and maintaining a custom model. Option D (Glue DataBrew) does not process PDF documents.

stem: A company has an application that stores user session data in Amazon DynamoDB with a TTL attribute set to expire sessions after 30 minutes. The company discovers that expired items are not being removed immediately, and the table is growing larger than expected. What should the solutions architect explain and recommend?

options.text: DynamoDB TTL removes expired items within 48 hours of expiration, not immediately. For applications requiring immediate session invalidation, the application should check the TTL attribute on read and treat expired items as invalid. To control table size, consider using a filter expression on queries to exclude expired items.
Increase the DynamoDB provisioned write capacity to speed up TTL deletions.
Create a Lambda function that runs every minute to scan and delete expired items.
Migrate to ElastiCache for Redis with built-in key expiration for immediate session removal.

explanation: DynamoDB TTL is a background process that removes expired items within 48 hours, not in real time. The application should treat items with past TTL timestamps as invalid on reads, using filter expressions. This is the expected behavior and does not require architectural changes. Option B (more capacity) does not affect TTL deletion speed since it is a background process. Option C (Lambda scan) adds cost and may interfere with DynamoDB's TTL process. Option D (ElastiCache migration) is an overreaction to understanding how TTL works.

stem: A company is modernizing a monolithic PHP application running on Apache. The application has a large codebase with interconnected modules. The company wants to gradually move to containers but cannot refactor the entire application at once. Which migration strategy allows the most gradual transition?

options.text: Containerize the monolith as-is using a single Docker image with Apache and PHP. Deploy on Amazon ECS. Then gradually extract individual modules into separate containers using the strangler fig pattern with an ALB routing traffic between the monolith and extracted services.
Rewrite the entire application in a modern language like Go and deploy as microservices on Amazon EKS.
Convert each PHP module into an AWS Lambda function using the Lambda custom runtime for PHP.
Deploy the PHP application on AWS Elastic Beanstalk without containerization.

explanation: Containerizing the monolith first (lift and shift) provides immediate benefits (consistent environments, scalability) without code changes. The strangler fig pattern then allows gradual extraction of modules into separate containers. The ALB routes requests between the monolith and new services based on URL patterns. This is the lowest-risk modernization path. Option B (full rewrite) is highest risk and takes the longest. Option C (Lambda per module) requires significant refactoring. Option D (Elastic Beanstalk) is not containerization and does not enable gradual decomposition.

stem: A company needs to ensure that all AWS Lambda functions across its organization are deployed within VPCs and that no Lambda function can be created without VPC configuration. This is required for compliance with the company's network security policy. Which enforcement mechanism should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Create an SCP that denies the lambda:CreateFunction and lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration actions unless the request includes VPC configuration parameters (lambda:VpcIds condition key).
Use AWS Config rules to detect Lambda functions without VPC configuration and delete them automatically.
Train developers to always include VPC configuration when creating Lambda functions.
Use AWS CloudFormation hooks to validate that all Lambda function resources include VPC configuration.

explanation: SCPs provide organization-wide preventive controls that cannot be bypassed. By denying Lambda function creation/updates without VPC configuration, no Lambda function can be deployed without VPC attachment. This enforces the network security policy at the API level. Option B is reactive. Option C relies on human behavior. Option D (CloudFormation hooks) only works for CloudFormation-based deployments, not CLI or SDK direct calls.

stem: A company is building a real-time bidding platform for online advertising that must respond to bid requests within 100 milliseconds. The platform receives 1 million bid requests per second and must evaluate user profiles, campaign rules, and budget constraints for each bid. Which architecture handles this throughput and latency requirement?

options.text: Use Network Load Balancer to distribute bid requests to a fleet of EC2 instances running custom bidding logic. Store user profiles and campaign data in Amazon ElastiCache for Redis for sub-millisecond lookups. Use DynamoDB for durable campaign and budget storage.
Use Amazon API Gateway with Lambda for processing bid requests and DynamoDB for user profile lookups.
Use Amazon CloudFront with Lambda@Edge for bid processing at edge locations.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to ingest bid requests and process them with Kinesis Data Analytics.

explanation: NLB provides ultra-low latency layer 4 load balancing for 1M TPS. EC2 instances with custom bidding logic provide deterministic processing time. ElastiCache for Redis provides sub-millisecond reads for user profiles and campaign data that must be evaluated within the 100ms budget. DynamoDB provides durable storage for budget tracking. Option B (API Gateway/Lambda) adds cold start latency and API Gateway overhead that may exceed 100ms at 1M TPS. Option C (Lambda@Edge) has execution time limitations. Option D (Kinesis) is for streaming analytics, not synchronous bid responses.

stem: A company's AWS infrastructure spans 5 Regions. The operations team uses Amazon CloudWatch dashboards to monitor each Region separately, creating delays in identifying cross-Region issues. They want a single dashboard showing metrics from all Regions. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Create a CloudWatch cross-account cross-Region dashboard in a central monitoring account that aggregates metrics from all 5 Regions using cross-Region metric data.
Use AWS CloudTrail to aggregate all operational metrics into a single Region.
Deploy a third-party monitoring tool on EC2 that polls CloudWatch APIs in each Region.
Replicate all CloudWatch metrics to a single Region using Kinesis Data Streams.

explanation: CloudWatch natively supports cross-account and cross-Region dashboards, allowing metrics from multiple Regions to be displayed on a single dashboard. This provides unified visibility without data replication. Option B (CloudTrail) logs API calls, not operational metrics. Option C (third-party tool) adds unnecessary cost and complexity. Option D (Kinesis replication) is overly complex for a dashboard use case.

stem: A company is implementing AWS Backup across its organization. All critical workloads in production accounts must be backed up daily with 30-day retention. The central operations team must manage backup policies, and workload account users must not be able to delete backups. Which configuration achieves this?

options.text: Enable AWS Backup with AWS Organizations support. Create backup policies in the management account and deploy them to production OUs. Store backups in a vault with a vault lock policy in compliance mode that prevents deletion.
Create individual backup plans in each production account and rely on account administrators to maintain them.
Use CloudFormation StackSets to deploy backup plans and manually copy backups to a central account.
Use AWS Lambda to create snapshots of all resources daily and store them in S3 with Object Lock.

explanation: AWS Backup with Organizations support allows centralized policy management. Backup policies deployed from the management account ensure consistent backup schedules across production accounts. Vault lock in compliance mode makes backups immutable, preventing even privileged users from deleting them. Option B relies on individual account management. Option C requires manual backup copying. Option D builds custom backup logic that duplicates AWS Backup functionality.

stem: A company is building a geospatial application that must find all restaurants within a 5-kilometer radius of a user's location. The database contains 10 million restaurant records with latitude/longitude coordinates. Queries must return results within 50 milliseconds. Which database solution should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon DynamoDB with a geospatial library that implements geohashing for the partition key, enabling efficient proximity queries with additional filtering.
Use Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL with the PostGIS extension, which provides native geospatial indexing and radius query functions (ST_DWithin).
Use Amazon OpenSearch Service with its built-in geo_distance query for proximity searches.
Use Amazon Neptune graph database to model relationships between users and nearby restaurants.

explanation: PostgreSQL with PostGIS provides native geospatial data types, spatial indexes (GiST), and functions like ST_DWithin for radius queries. It efficiently handles 10 million records with proper indexing and returns results within 50ms. PostGIS is the industry standard for geospatial queries. Option A (DynamoDB with geohashing) works but is more complex and less optimized for true radius queries. Option C (OpenSearch) supports geo queries but is primarily a search engine. Option D (Neptune) is a graph database not optimized for geographic proximity queries.

stem: A company wants to migrate its on-premises Kubernetes workloads to AWS. The team has extensive Kubernetes experience and uses Helm charts for application deployment. They need to maintain compatibility with their existing Kubernetes manifests and tooling. Which migration approach requires the least changes?

options.text: Use Amazon EKS to create a managed Kubernetes cluster. Apply existing Kubernetes manifests and Helm charts with only endpoint and storage class changes. Use the AWS Load Balancer Controller for service exposure.
Use Amazon ECS with the ECS CLI and convert all Kubernetes manifests to ECS task definitions.
Use AWS App Runner to deploy containerized applications without Kubernetes.
Deploy Kubernetes manually on EC2 instances using kubeadm for full control.

explanation: Amazon EKS is a managed Kubernetes service fully compatible with standard Kubernetes APIs, kubectl, and Helm. Existing manifests and Helm charts can be applied with minimal changes (primarily storage classes and service annotations for AWS integrations). The AWS Load Balancer Controller handles ALB/NLB provisioning through Kubernetes ingress resources. Option B (ECS) requires converting all Kubernetes manifests. Option C (App Runner) does not support Kubernetes. Option D (kubeadm on EC2) lacks managed control plane benefits.

stem: A company has an application that uses Amazon S3 for storage with versioning enabled. Over time, the bucket has accumulated millions of non-current versions and delete markers, significantly increasing storage costs. How should the solutions architect reduce costs while maintaining the current version of all objects?

options.text: Create an S3 Lifecycle policy with a NoncurrentVersionExpiration rule that deletes non-current versions after 30 days, and an ExpiredObjectDeleteMarker rule that removes expired delete markers.
Disable versioning on the bucket to stop accumulating non-current versions.
Use S3 Inventory to list all versions and write a script to delete non-current versions manually.
Move the entire bucket to S3 Glacier to reduce storage costs for all versions.

explanation: S3 Lifecycle policies with NoncurrentVersionExpiration automatically delete old non-current versions after a specified number of days, reducing storage costs. ExpiredObjectDeleteMarker removes orphaned delete markers. This preserves current versions while cleaning up historical versions. Option B (disable versioning) does not clean up existing non-current versions and loses version protection. Option C (manual script) is labor-intensive and does not automate ongoing cleanup. Option D (Glacier) reduces cost but makes all data inaccessible for immediate retrieval.

stem: A company needs to establish connectivity between its AWS VPCs and Microsoft Azure VNets. The company has workloads in both clouds and requires private, low-latency communication between them. Data must not traverse the public internet. Which TWO components should the solutions architect configure? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Establish an AWS Direct Connect connection to a colocation facility that also hosts an Azure ExpressRoute circuit, and use a private peering between them.
Configure AWS Site-to-Site VPN with Azure VPN Gateway for encrypted connectivity between the AWS VPC and Azure VNet.
Use AWS Transit Gateway to centralize the Azure connectivity for multiple VPCs on the AWS side.
Use AWS PrivateLink to expose AWS services to Azure VNets directly.
Use Amazon Route 53 to resolve DNS names between AWS and Azure environments.

explanation: Direct Connect to a shared colocation facility with Azure ExpressRoute (A) provides private, low-latency connectivity that avoids the public internet. Transit Gateway (C) centralizes this Azure connectivity, allowing multiple AWS VPCs to access Azure through a single connection point. Option B (VPN) traverses the public internet, violating the requirement. Option D (PrivateLink) is for intra-AWS service access. Option E (Route 53) handles DNS but not network connectivity.

stem: A company is designing a data pipeline that processes financial transactions for regulatory reporting. The pipeline must guarantee exactly-once processing semantics, maintain strict ordering of transactions per account, and produce audit trails showing every processing step. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with enhanced fan-out for ordered ingestion per account (using account ID as partition key). Process with AWS Lambda with event source mapping that guarantees ordered processing per shard. Use AWS Step Functions for multi-step processing with audit logging to CloudWatch.
Use Amazon SQS Standard queue for ingestion and Lambda for processing with DynamoDB for deduplication.
Use Amazon MSK with Kafka transactions for exactly-once semantics and consumer groups for processing.
Use Amazon EventBridge for event ingestion with Lambda targets for processing.

explanation: Kinesis partitions by account ID ensuring per-account ordering. Lambda event source mappings process records in order within each shard. Step Functions provide detailed execution history for audit trails with built-in logging. Enhanced fan-out provides dedicated throughput. Option B (SQS Standard) does not guarantee ordering. Option C (MSK) provides exactly-once but requires managing infrastructure. Option D (EventBridge) does not guarantee ordering.

stem: A company is migrating its on-premises data center to AWS. The data center has 80 physical servers with various interdependencies. The company needs to understand these dependencies before planning migration waves. Which approach should the solutions architect recommend for discovery?

options.text: Deploy AWS Application Discovery Service agents on all servers to collect configuration data, network connections, and running processes. Use AWS Migration Hub to visualize server dependencies and group servers into migration waves.
Review existing network documentation and interview application owners to understand dependencies.
Use nmap to scan the network and identify active connections between servers.
Migrate all 80 servers simultaneously to avoid dependency issues.

explanation: Application Discovery Service agents collect detailed data including running processes, network connections (source/destination/port), and resource utilization. Migration Hub visualizes these dependencies, enabling informed grouping into migration waves. Servers with strong dependencies can be grouped together for coordinated migration. Option B (manual review) is incomplete and error-prone. Option C (nmap) provides point-in-time network data but misses process-level dependencies. Option D (simultaneous migration) is extremely risky for 80 interdependent servers.

stem: A company has an application deployed using AWS Elastic Beanstalk with a Classic Load Balancer. The application serves HTTPS traffic but the TLS certificate is expiring soon. The company wants to simplify certificate management going forward. What should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Migrate from Classic Load Balancer to Application Load Balancer. Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to provision and manage the TLS certificate. ACM automatically renews certificates before expiration.
Purchase a new certificate from a commercial CA and manually install it on the Classic Load Balancer.
Terminate TLS on the EC2 instances behind the load balancer using self-signed certificates.
Use CloudFront in front of the Elastic Beanstalk environment and manage the certificate on CloudFront.

explanation: Migrating to ALB enables using ACM for free, auto-renewing TLS certificates. ACM handles certificate provisioning, validation, and renewal automatically, eliminating manual certificate management. ALB also provides advanced features like path-based routing and WebSocket support. Option B requires manual renewal every time the certificate expires. Option C (self-signed) is not trusted by browsers. Option D adds CloudFront complexity when the load balancer can handle TLS directly.

stem: A company has an AWS Organization with 150 accounts. The company needs to ensure that no one, including root users, can disable CloudTrail logging in any member account. Which control provides this guarantee?

options.text: Create an SCP that denies cloudtrail:StopLogging, cloudtrail:DeleteTrail, and cloudtrail:UpdateTrail actions for all principals. Attach the SCP to the root OU. Note that SCPs do not apply to the management account.
Enable CloudTrail log file integrity validation to detect any tampering with logs.
Configure IAM policies in each account that deny CloudTrail modification.
Use AWS Config rules to detect CloudTrail being disabled and re-enable it automatically.

explanation: SCPs override all IAM permissions in member accounts, including root user permissions. Denying CloudTrail stop, delete, and update actions prevents anyone in member accounts from disabling logging. This is the strongest preventive control. Option B (log integrity) detects tampering after the fact but does not prevent disabling CloudTrail. Option C (IAM policies) can be overridden by root users. Option D (Config/auto-remediation) is reactive, leaving a gap between disabling and re-enabling.

stem: A company is building an application that needs to send 10 million push notifications within a 30-minute window during daily sales events. The notifications must be personalized based on user preferences and purchase history. Which architecture supports this throughput?

options.text: Use Amazon Pinpoint with campaigns targeting user segments. Pinpoint handles the high-throughput delivery across push notification platforms (APNs, FCM) with personalized message templates.
Use Amazon SNS mobile push to send notifications individually to each device token via Lambda functions.
Build a custom push notification service on EC2 that connects to APNs and FCM directly.
Use Amazon SES to send email notifications instead of push notifications.

explanation: Amazon Pinpoint is designed for high-throughput, personalized messaging campaigns. It handles the complexity of connecting to multiple push platforms (APNs for iOS, FCM for Android), supports message personalization with user attributes, and scales to millions of messages. Campaign scheduling ensures delivery within the 30-minute window. Option B (SNS) supports push but lacks built-in personalization and campaign management at this scale. Option C (custom service) requires managing connections to push platforms. Option D (SES) sends email, not push notifications.

stem: A company has a large on-premises data warehouse using Netezza appliances. The warehouse stores 100 TB of data and processes complex analytical queries with 100+ concurrent users. The company wants to migrate to a cloud-native solution with better scalability. Which target platform should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Amazon Redshift with RA3 nodes for compute-storage separation. Use AWS SCT for schema conversion from Netezza to Redshift, and AWS DMS for data migration. Enable Redshift concurrency scaling for handling 100+ concurrent users.
Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL because it is compatible with Netezza SQL.
Amazon Athena with data stored in S3 for serverless analytics.
Amazon EMR with Apache Hive for data warehousing queries.

explanation: Redshift is Amazon's data warehouse service optimized for complex analytical queries. RA3 nodes separate compute from storage for independent scaling. SCT converts Netezza-specific SQL and schema to Redshift-compatible format. DMS migrates the data. Concurrency scaling automatically adds compute for 100+ concurrent users during peak. Option B (Aurora) is OLTP, not OLAP optimized. Option C (Athena) is for ad-hoc queries and may not match Netezza performance for complex analytical workloads. Option D (EMR/Hive) requires managing clusters.

stem: A company runs a web application behind an Application Load Balancer. The security team requires that the application only accepts traffic from specific countries, blocks known malicious IP addresses, and limits the request rate to prevent DDoS attacks. Which TWO services should the solutions architect configure? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Configure AWS WAF on the ALB with geo-match conditions to allow only specific countries, IP set rules to block known malicious IPs, and rate-based rules to limit request rates.
Enable AWS Shield Advanced for DDoS protection with automatic application layer mitigation.
Configure VPC Network ACLs to block traffic from specific countries.
Use Amazon CloudFront geo-restriction to block non-approved countries.
Deploy a third-party firewall appliance on EC2 in front of the ALB.

explanation: WAF (A) provides all three required capabilities: geo-match conditions for country-based filtering, IP set rules for blocking known malicious IPs, and rate-based rules for request rate limiting. Shield Advanced (B) adds DDoS protection with automatic application layer mitigation, which works with WAF rules to respond to detected attacks. Option C (NACLs) cannot filter by country. Option D (CloudFront geo-restriction) only blocks countries at the CDN level and the question does not mention CloudFront. Option E (third-party firewall) adds cost and complexity.

stem: A company wants to ensure that all Amazon RDS instances across its organization use encryption at rest with customer managed KMS keys. The company also needs to prevent the creation of RDS instances that use the default AWS managed key. Which solution should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Create an SCP that allows rds:CreateDBInstance only when the rds:StorageEncrypted condition is true and the kms:ViaService condition specifies an approved customer managed key ARN.
Use AWS Config rules to detect unencrypted RDS instances and notify the team.
Create IAM policies in each account that require encryption for RDS creation.
Enable RDS encryption by default in each account's RDS settings.

explanation: An SCP with conditions on rds:StorageEncrypted and the KMS key ARN prevents creation of unencrypted RDS instances or instances using the default AWS managed key. This is a preventive control at the organization level that cannot be bypassed. Option B (Config) is detective, not preventive. Option C (IAM policies) can be changed by account administrators. Option D (default encryption) enables encryption but allows the default AWS managed key, not a customer managed key.

stem: A healthcare company needs to build a HIPAA-compliant telemedicine platform that supports real-time video consultations between doctors and patients. The platform must record all consultations for compliance, store recordings securely, and support up to 10,000 concurrent video sessions. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon Chime SDK for real-time video communication. Configure media capture pipelines to record sessions to Amazon S3 with server-side encryption. Store recordings in S3 with Object Lock for compliance retention.
Deploy a WebRTC server on EC2 instances with TURN relay servers for video communication and store recordings on EBS volumes.
Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams for real-time video and recording with HLS playback.
Use AWS Elemental MediaLive for video broadcasting and MediaPackage for delivery.

explanation: Amazon Chime SDK provides a HIPAA-eligible real-time video communication service that scales to 10,000+ concurrent sessions. Media capture pipelines automatically record sessions to S3. S3 encryption and Object Lock provide secure, immutable storage for compliance. Option B (WebRTC on EC2) requires managing signaling servers, TURN servers, and recording infrastructure. Option C (Kinesis Video Streams) is for IoT video ingestion, not interactive video calls. Option D (MediaLive/MediaPackage) is for broadcasting, not two-way video communication.

stem: A company has an existing REST API built with Amazon API Gateway and Lambda. The API is experiencing high latency (2-3 seconds) for complex queries that join data from DynamoDB and an external third-party API. Users expect sub-second responses. The third-party API data changes daily. Which optimization should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Cache the third-party API data in DynamoDB with a 24-hour TTL (matching the daily update cycle). Modify the Lambda function to read all data from DynamoDB, eliminating the external API call latency. Enable API Gateway caching for frequently requested queries.
Increase the Lambda function memory to speed up processing.
Replace Lambda with EC2 instances for consistent performance.
Add CloudFront in front of API Gateway to cache responses at edge locations.

explanation: Caching third-party API data in DynamoDB eliminates the slowest part of the query (external API call). Since the data changes daily, a 24-hour TTL keeps the cache fresh. Reading from DynamoDB provides single-digit millisecond latency. API Gateway caching further reduces latency for repeated queries. Option B (more memory) slightly improves Lambda performance but does not address external API latency. Option C (EC2) does not solve the external API latency. Option D (CloudFront) helps with caching but the origin latency remains high for non-cached requests.

stem: A company is migrating a complex microservices application from on-premises Docker Compose to AWS. The application has 15 services with complex inter-service dependencies defined in docker-compose.yml files.
