This heartbeat mechanism prevents reprocessing while allowing timely redelivery of truly failed messages.
Delete messages immediately upon receipt before processing begins.
Set the visibility timeout to 24 hours to ensure no message is reprocessed.
Use FIFO queues to prevent duplicate processing.

explanation: Setting the visibility timeout longer than the maximum processing time (35 > 30 minutes) prevents most reprocessing. The ChangeMessageVisibility heartbeat pattern extends the timeout dynamically for long-running messages, providing a safety net without over-provisioning the timeout. Option B (immediate delete) loses messages if processing fails. Option C (24-hour timeout) delays redelivery of genuinely failed messages for too long. Option D (FIFO) prevents duplicate delivery but has throughput limitations.

stem: A company has a data center with 200 physical servers running VMware vSphere. The company wants to evaluate which workloads are suitable for migration to AWS and estimate the total cost of ownership (TCO) on AWS. The company needs to complete this assessment in 2 weeks without installing agents on production servers. Which approach should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use AWS Application Discovery Service in agentless mode with the Discovery Connector deployed as a virtual appliance in the VMware environment. The connector collects VM configuration, utilization, and performance data from vCenter without installing agents on VMs. Import the discovery data into AWS Migration Hub for application grouping and dependency visualization. Use the AWS Migration Evaluator (formerly TSO Logic) to generate a detailed TCO comparison and optimization recommendations.
Install the Application Discovery Agent on all 200 servers for detailed analysis.
Manually inventory all servers and estimate costs using the AWS Pricing Calculator.
Use AWS Server Migration Service to start migrating and assess costs afterward.

explanation: The agentless Discovery Connector runs as a vCenter VM appliance, collecting data from all VMs without touching production servers. This meets the 2-week timeline and no-agent constraint. Migration Hub visualizes groupings. Migration Evaluator provides TCO analysis with right-sizing recommendations. Option B (agents) requires installation on each server, which was explicitly not desired. Option C (manual inventory) is time-consuming and error-prone. Option D (SMS migration) is premature without assessment.

stem: A company is building a financial reconciliation system that must compare millions of transaction records between two systems daily. Records must be matched based on multiple fields (amount, date, reference number) with configurable matching tolerance. Unmatched records must be flagged for manual review. The system must handle 10 million records per system. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Load transaction records from both systems into Amazon S3 in Parquet format. Use AWS Glue ETL with PySpark for the matching logic, implementing fuzzy matching and tolerance-based comparisons using broadcast joins for the smaller dataset. Store matched and unmatched results in separate S3 locations. Use Amazon Athena for ad-hoc analysis of unmatched records. Trigger the reconciliation workflow daily using Amazon EventBridge Scheduler with Step Functions orchestration.
Load all records into Amazon RDS for MySQL and use SQL JOIN queries for matching.
Use AWS Lambda to compare records one at a time from both systems.
Import records into Amazon DynamoDB and use scan operations for matching.

explanation: Glue with PySpark handles 10M records efficiently using distributed processing and broadcast joins. Parquet format enables columnar reads for specific matching fields. S3 provides cost-effective storage. Athena enables serverless analysis of unmatched records. EventBridge with Step Functions automates the daily workflow. Option B (RDS) may struggle with 10M-record joins. Option C (Lambda one-at-a-time) is extremely slow for millions of records. Option D (DynamoDB scan) is expensive and slow for full-table comparisons.

stem: A company is operating a centralized data analytics platform that serves data to 500 internal users. The platform uses Amazon Redshift and Amazon QuickSight. The company needs to implement row-level security so that users from different departments can only see data relevant to their department, without creating separate tables or views for each department. Which solution should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Implement Redshift Row-Level Security (RLS) policies that filter rows based on the current session user's department attribute. Create RLS policies that match the department column in data tables against the user's department stored in a lookup table. In QuickSight, configure SAML-based SSO with department attribute passed as a session tag. Use QuickSight row-level security datasets that map users to their allowed department data.
Create separate Redshift schemas for each department with their own copies of data.
Use Redshift views with WHERE clauses for each department.
Implement application-level filtering in QuickSight by creating separate dashboards for each department.

explanation: Redshift RLS policies enforce row-level filtering transparently at the database level without maintaining separate tables or views. Session-based filtering uses the authenticated user's department attribute. QuickSight RLS provides an additional layer of security at the visualization level. SAML SSO passes department attributes automatically. Option B (separate schemas) requires data duplication. Option C (views per department) requires maintaining one view per department per table. Option D (separate dashboards) requires maintaining 500+ dashboard variants.

stem: A company runs a web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The application uses sticky sessions (session affinity) which prevents the ALB from distributing load evenly. Some instances are overloaded while others are idle. The company wants to maintain session state while improving load distribution. How should the solutions architect redesign the session management?

options.text: Remove ALB sticky sessions and externalize session state to Amazon ElastiCache for Redis. Store session data in Redis with a TTL matching the session timeout. Update the application to read and write session data to Redis using the session ID from a cookie. This allows any instance to serve any request, enabling the ALB to distribute load evenly while maintaining session continuity.
Increase the number of EC2 instances to handle the uneven load.
Switch to a Network Load Balancer for better load distribution.
Use CloudFront to cache session data at the edge.

explanation: Externalizing session state to Redis eliminates the need for sticky sessions, allowing the ALB to distribute requests evenly across all instances. Any instance can handle any request by retrieving session data from Redis. Redis provides microsecond latency for session reads/writes. TTL-based expiration manages session lifecycle. Option B (more instances) adds cost without fixing the distribution problem. Option C (NLB) operates at Layer 4 and does not improve session management. Option D (CloudFront) is not designed for session state management.

stem: A company is modernizing a legacy reporting system that generates 500 complex PDF reports nightly. Each report queries a database, processes data with custom business logic, and renders a multi-page PDF. The current system runs on a single server and takes 8 hours to complete. The company wants to reduce processing time to under 1 hour. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use AWS Step Functions with a Map state to parallelize report generation across 500 concurrent executions. Each execution uses a Lambda function to query Amazon Aurora for report data, process business logic, and invoke a second Lambda function with container image packaging (including PDF rendering libraries) to generate the PDF. Store generated PDFs in Amazon S3. Use Step Functions Distributed Map for large-scale parallel processing with batching and error handling.
Deploy a larger EC2 instance with more CPU cores to speed up sequential processing.
Use Amazon EMR to process all reports using Apache Spark.
Schedule 500 separate EventBridge rules, one for each report.

explanation: Step Functions Distributed Map parallelizes 500 report generations across concurrent Lambda executions, reducing 8 hours of sequential work to minutes. Container image packaging supports PDF rendering libraries (like wkhtmltopdf, Puppeteer) that may exceed Lambda layer size limits. Aurora provides the database backend. S3 stores generated PDFs. Option B (bigger EC2) provides limited speedup for sequential processing. Option C (EMR Spark) is not designed for PDF rendering. Option D (500 EventBridge rules) lacks orchestration and error handling.

stem: A company is building a customer identity and access management (CIAM) system for a consumer-facing application with 10 million users. The system must support social login (Google, Facebook, Apple), email/password authentication, MFA, and progressive profiling. User profiles must be accessible with sub-5ms latency. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon Cognito User Pools for user authentication with social identity providers (Google, Facebook, Apple) configured as federation providers. Enable adaptive MFA based on risk assessment. Use Cognito Lambda triggers (Pre-Sign-Up, Post-Confirmation, Pre-Token-Generation) for progressive profiling and custom claims. Store extended user profiles in Amazon DynamoDB with DAX for sub-millisecond read latency. Use Cognito Hosted UI for a consistent, customizable login experience.
Build a custom authentication system using Lambda functions and DynamoDB.
Use AWS IAM Identity Center for consumer-facing authentication.
Deploy Keycloak on Amazon EKS for identity management.

explanation: Cognito User Pools provide managed CIAM with built-in social login, MFA, and customizable authentication flows. Lambda triggers enable progressive profiling (collecting additional profile data over time). DynamoDB with DAX provides sub-millisecond reads for 10M user profiles. Hosted UI provides a consistent login experience. Option B (custom auth) requires implementing security features from scratch. Option C (IAM Identity Center) is for workforce, not consumer identity. Option D (Keycloak on EKS) requires infrastructure management.

stem: A company operates an AWS environment where development teams frequently create and forget about resources, leading to significant cost waste. The company estimates 30% of their AWS spend is on unused or underutilized resources. The company needs an automated solution to identify and clean up waste. Which solution should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Deploy AWS Cost Anomaly Detection for spending alerts. Use AWS Compute Optimizer to identify underutilized EC2, EBS, and Lambda resources. Create automated cleanup workflows using AWS Systems Manager Automation documents that identify unattached EBS volumes, stopped EC2 instances older than 7 days, unused Elastic IPs, and idle load balancers. Trigger these automations weekly via EventBridge Scheduler. Implement mandatory resource tagging with tag policies and auto-terminate resources without required tags after a grace period.
Reduce all account budgets by 30% to force teams to optimize.
Manually review AWS billing dashboards monthly to identify waste.
Restrict all teams to only t3.micro instances to limit spending.

explanation: Cost Anomaly Detection catches spending spikes early. Compute Optimizer identifies right-sizing opportunities. Systems Manager Automation provides automated cleanup of common waste patterns (unattached EBS, stopped instances, unused EIPs). EventBridge Scheduler ensures regular execution. Tag policies enforce resource ownership, enabling accountability. Option B (budget cuts) may impact legitimate workloads. Option C (monthly review) is reactive and delayed. Option D (instance restrictions) prevents legitimate use cases.

stem: A company uses Amazon CloudWatch to monitor their AWS infrastructure. The operations team receives over 1,000 alarm notifications daily, causing alert fatigue and missed critical issues. Most alarms are for non-critical metrics that briefly exceed thresholds before returning to normal. How should the solutions architect reduce noise while ensuring critical issues are caught?

options.text: Implement CloudWatch composite alarms that combine multiple metric alarms using AND/OR logic to reduce false positives. Use CloudWatch anomaly detection with band-based alarms instead of static thresholds to account for normal metric variation. Configure alarm actions to route through Amazon SNS topics with different severity levels. Use CloudWatch Alarm suppressor rules to suppress alarms during planned maintenance windows.
Delete all existing alarms and start from scratch.
Increase all alarm thresholds by 50% to reduce the number of triggering events.
Route all alarms to a single email distribution list and let the team filter manually.

explanation: Composite alarms reduce false positives by requiring multiple conditions to be met simultaneously. Anomaly detection adapts to normal patterns, eliminating alarms from expected metric variations. Severity-based routing ensures critical alarms get immediate attention. Maintenance suppressors prevent expected alarm noise. Option B (delete all) risks missing critical issues during reconfiguration. Option C (raise thresholds) may miss genuine problems. Option D (single email) increases noise for all recipients.

stem: A company is migrating an application that uses Redis as a primary database (not just a cache) with persistence enabled. The Redis cluster stores 500 GB of data with complex data structures (sorted sets, hyperloglogs, streams). The company needs a fully managed solution on AWS that supports all Redis data structures. Which migration approach should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Migrate to Amazon ElastiCache for Redis with cluster mode enabled. Use the r6g.2xlarge node type for memory-optimized performance. Enable Multi-AZ with automatic failover for high availability. Configure AOF (Append-Only File) persistence for data durability. Use the Redis SLAVEOF/REPLICAOF command during migration for online data transfer with minimal downtime. After synchronization, promote the ElastiCache cluster and cut over.

Migrate to Amazon MemoryDB for Redis, which provides a durable, Redis-compatible database with microsecond read latency and Multi-AZ durability using a distributed transaction log. MemoryDB is designed specifically for primary database use with all Redis data structures supported.
Migrate to Amazon DynamoDB and rewrite the data model from Redis data structures.
Deploy Redis on EC2 instances and manage it manually.

explanation: MemoryDB for Redis is purpose-built as a durable primary database (not cache) with Redis compatibility. It uses a distributed transaction log for Multi-AZ durability, ensuring no data loss. It supports all Redis data structures and commands. ElastiCache (Option A) is primarily designed as a cache with optional persistence that may lose data during failover. Option C (DynamoDB) requires complete data model rewrite. Option D (EC2 Redis) requires operational management.

stem: A company is building a platform for processing and analyzing satellite imagery. Each image is 2 GB in size, and the platform processes 1,000 images daily. Processing includes image segmentation, object detection, and change detection. Results must be queryable through a REST API. Which TWO components should the solutions architect include in the architecture? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Use Amazon SageMaker Processing jobs with GPU-accelerated instances (ml.p3 or ml.g4dn) for image segmentation and object detection. SageMaker Processing provides managed infrastructure that starts and stops per job, optimizing costs for the batch processing pattern.

Store raw satellite images in Amazon S3 with S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Store processing results in Amazon DynamoDB for the REST API queries. Use Amazon API Gateway with Lambda to serve the query results from DynamoDB.
Use AWS Lambda for all image processing tasks.
Store all images and results in Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL.
Use Amazon Rekognition for satellite image object detection.

explanation: SageMaker Processing (Option A) provides managed GPU compute for ML-based image processing (segmentation, object detection) with per-job scaling. S3 with Intelligent-Tiering (Option B) provides cost-effective storage for 2 TB of daily images. DynamoDB with API Gateway and Lambda provides a scalable REST API for query results. Option C (Lambda) is limited to 10 GB memory and 15-minute timeout, insufficient for 2 GB image processing. Option D (RDS) is not designed for binary image storage at scale. Option E (Rekognition) is trained on common objects, not satellite imagery.

stem: A company with a multi-account AWS environment needs to share VPC subnets from a central networking account with workload accounts. The shared subnets must be used by resources in the workload accounts, but workload accounts should not be able to modify the subnet configurations, route tables, or security group rules of the shared subnets. Which solution should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Use AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) to share subnets from the networking account with workload accounts through the AWS Organization. RAM subnet sharing allows workload accounts to deploy resources (EC2, RDS, ECS, Lambda) into the shared subnets while keeping subnet administration (route tables, NACLs, subnet configuration) controlled by the networking account. Workload accounts can create their own security groups for resources in shared subnets.
Create VPC peering connections and allow workload accounts to use CIDR ranges from the central VPC.
Copy subnet configurations to each workload account using CloudFormation StackSets.
Grant workload accounts IAM cross-account access to manage the networking account's VPC.

explanation: RAM subnet sharing provides the exact security model needed: workload accounts can deploy resources in shared subnets and create their own security groups, but cannot modify subnet configurations, route tables, or NACLs, which remain under the networking account's control. This is the standard pattern for centralized network management. Option B (VPC peering) does not share subnets. Option C (StackSets copy) creates separate subnets, not shared ones. Option D (cross-account IAM) grants too much access to networking resources.

stem: A company's application uses Amazon S3 for storing user-uploaded files. The application generates presigned URLs for upload and download operations. Users report that downloads of large files (1-5 GB) frequently fail with timeout errors, especially in regions with poor network connectivity. How should the solutions architect improve the reliability of large file transfers?

options.text: Implement S3 Transfer Acceleration for all upload and download operations to improve transfer speeds over long distances. For large file downloads, use S3 byte-range fetches to download files in parallel chunks, with automatic retry logic for failed chunks. For uploads, use S3 multipart upload with the AWS SDK, which automatically handles chunking, parallelization, and retry of failed parts. Set appropriate content-disposition headers for download resumability.
Increase the presigned URL expiration time to 24 hours.
Move all files to Amazon EFS and serve them directly from EC2 instances.
Compress all files before upload to reduce file sizes.

explanation: Transfer Acceleration uses CloudFront's edge network for faster long-distance transfers. Byte-range fetches enable parallel downloading with individual chunk retries, preventing full restart on failure. Multipart upload breaks large files into manageable parts with per-part retry. These address both speed and reliability for large files. Option B (longer expiration) does not improve transfer reliability. Option C (EFS) requires managing EC2 instances. Option D (compression) may not work for all file types (images, videos) and adds processing overhead.

stem: A company has a legacy application using an Oracle RAC (Real Application Clusters) database for high availability with shared storage. The application requires multi-node read-write access to the same database. The company wants to migrate to AWS while maintaining similar high availability characteristics. Which target database architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Migrate to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with Multi-AZ and Global Database. Aurora provides a single writer with up to 15 read replicas sharing the same distributed storage volume. For write scaling, implement application-level sharding or use Aurora Serverless v2 for automatic compute scaling. Use AWS SCT to convert Oracle RAC-specific SQL and PL/SQL to PostgreSQL equivalents.
Deploy Oracle RAC on Amazon EC2 instances with shared EBS volumes.
Use Amazon RDS for Oracle with Multi-AZ for a managed Oracle solution.
Migrate to Amazon DynamoDB for multi-node write access.

explanation: Aurora provides high availability comparable to Oracle RAC with Multi-AZ and shared distributed storage. While Aurora uses a single-writer model (unlike RAC's multi-writer), its distributed storage layer and fast failover (typically under 30 seconds) provide similar availability guarantees. SCT handles Oracle-to-PostgreSQL conversion. Aurora Serverless v2 scales compute automatically. Option B (Oracle RAC on EC2) does not reduce licensing costs or operational overhead. Option C (RDS Oracle) still requires Oracle licenses. Option D (DynamoDB) is not a relational database replacement.

stem: A company is designing a system for processing customer support tickets using AI. The system must classify tickets by urgency and category, extract key entities (product names, order numbers), suggest responses based on similar past tickets, and route to the appropriate support team. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon Comprehend for ticket classification (custom classifier trained on historical tickets) and entity extraction (custom entity recognizer for product names, order numbers). Use Amazon Kendra to search similar past tickets and suggested responses from a knowledge base indexed from historical ticket resolutions. Route tickets based on classification results using Amazon EventBridge rules to appropriate SQS queues per support team. Use Amazon Bedrock for generating response suggestions when similar tickets are not found.
Build a custom NLP pipeline using Amazon SageMaker for all text processing tasks.
Use keyword matching with Lambda functions to classify and route tickets.
Send all tickets to a single support queue and let agents manually classify them.

explanation: Comprehend provides managed NLP for classification (custom classifiers) and entity extraction (custom entity recognizers) without building custom models. Kendra provides intelligent search for similar past tickets. EventBridge rules automate routing based on classification. Bedrock generates AI-powered response suggestions. Option B (custom SageMaker) requires ML expertise and model maintenance. Option C (keyword matching) lacks understanding of context and nuance. Option D (manual classification) does not scale and is inconsistent.

stem: A company operates a SaaS platform serving 1,000 customers. Each customer must be able to connect their AWS account to the platform for resource monitoring. The platform needs read-only access to EC2, RDS, and S3 resources in each customer account. The company wants to implement the most secure cross-account access pattern. Which solution should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Create a CloudFormation template that customers deploy in their accounts. The template creates an IAM role with a trust policy that allows the SaaS platform's AWS account to assume the role, with an external ID unique to each customer. The role's permission policy grants read-only access to EC2, RDS, and S3. The external ID prevents the confused deputy problem. Customers provide their role ARN and the platform uses STS AssumeRole to access their resources.
Ask customers to create IAM users with access keys and share them with the SaaS platform.
Use a single IAM role that all 1,000 customer accounts trust.
Ask customers to grant access through S3 bucket policies and EC2 resource policies.

explanation: IAM cross-account roles with external IDs is the AWS-recommended pattern for SaaS cross-account access. External IDs prevent the confused deputy attack where a malicious customer tricks the platform into accessing another customer's account. CloudFormation templates standardize the setup. STS AssumeRole provides temporary credentials. Option B (access keys) creates long-term credentials that are harder to manage and rotate. Option C (single role) does not distinguish between customers. Option D (resource policies) is limited and does not cover all services.

stem: A company runs a data warehouse on Amazon Redshift with 50 users running concurrent queries. Query performance has degraded because user-created tables lack proper sort keys, distribution styles, and compression encodings. The team does not have time to manually optimize all tables. How should the solutions architect improve performance?

options.text: Enable Amazon Redshift automatic table optimization (ATO). ATO automatically applies sort keys and distribution styles based on query patterns without manual intervention. Enable automatic compression encoding on new tables. Use Redshift Advisor to get recommendations for existing queries and table designs. Additionally, enable concurrency scaling to automatically add cluster capacity when 50 concurrent queries create queuing.
Recreate all tables with manually chosen sort keys and distribution styles.
Double the number of Redshift nodes to handle the query load.
Migrate from Redshift to Amazon Athena for all queries.

explanation: ATO automatically analyzes query patterns and applies optimal sort keys and distribution styles without manual work. Automatic compression encoding optimizes storage and I/O. Redshift Advisor provides actionable recommendations. Concurrency scaling elastically handles query spikes from 50 concurrent users. Option B (manual optimization) requires significant time and expertise. Option C (more nodes) increases cost without fixing the underlying optimization issues. Option D (Athena migration) requires significant migration effort.

stem: A company is building a platform for real-time sports analytics. The platform must ingest player tracking data from 100 sensors at 100 Hz (10,000 data points per second per sensor), compute aggregate statistics (speed, distance, acceleration) in real time, and display results on a dashboard with sub-second refresh. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with multiple shards to ingest 1 million data points per second. Deploy a Kinesis Data Analytics (Apache Flink) application to compute real-time aggregate statistics using tumbling and sliding windows. Write computed metrics to Amazon Timestream for time-series storage and historical analysis. Serve the dashboard through Amazon Managed Grafana connected to Timestream for real-time visualization with sub-second refresh.
Use Amazon SQS to buffer sensor data and process it with Lambda functions.
Store all sensor data in Amazon S3 and use Athena for real-time analytics.
Use Amazon DynamoDB Streams to process sensor data in real time.

explanation: Kinesis Data Streams handles millions of records per second for high-throughput ingestion. Kinesis Data Analytics (Flink) provides real-time stream processing with windowed aggregations for statistics computation. Timestream is purpose-built for time-series data with built-in time-series functions. Managed Grafana provides real-time dashboards with sub-second refresh from Timestream. Option B (SQS + Lambda) adds latency and is not designed for ordered stream processing. Option C (S3 + Athena) is batch-oriented. Option D (DynamoDB Streams) is event-driven, not stream processing.

stem: A company is consolidating security operations across 500 AWS accounts. The security team needs a single pane of glass that aggregates security findings from multiple sources (GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, IAM Access Analyzer, Firewall Manager) and enables automated response workflows. Which solution should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Deploy AWS Security Hub as the central aggregation point with a delegated administrator account. Enable all AWS security service integrations. Configure security standards (CIS AWS Foundations, PCI DSS, AWS Foundational Security Best Practices). Use Security Hub custom actions with EventBridge to trigger Lambda-based automated remediation workflows for critical findings. Create custom insights for organization-specific security metrics.
Build a custom security dashboard using CloudWatch dashboards aggregating metrics from all accounts.
Deploy a third-party SIEM on EC2 instances to aggregate findings from all services.
Use AWS Systems Manager OpsCenter to manage security findings across accounts.

explanation: Security Hub provides native aggregation of findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, IAM Access Analyzer, and Firewall Manager in a standardized format (ASFF). Delegated administrator enables organization-wide management. Security standards provide compliance scoring. Custom actions with EventBridge enable automated remediation. Custom insights provide organization-specific views. Option B (CloudWatch) does not aggregate security findings. Option C (third-party SIEM) adds cost and operational overhead. Option D (OpsCenter) is for operational issues, not security aggregation.

stem: A company's application uses Amazon DynamoDB with provisioned capacity. The table receives steady traffic of 5,000 WCU during business hours (8 AM - 8 PM) and drops to 500 WCU overnight. The company currently provisions 5,000 WCU 24/7, paying for unused capacity overnight. How should the solutions architect optimize costs?

options.text: Enable DynamoDB Auto Scaling with a target utilization of 70%. Set the minimum capacity to 500 WCU and maximum to 7,000 WCU. Configure Application Auto Scaling scheduled actions to pre-scale to 5,000 WCU at 7:45 AM before traffic increases, preventing throttling during the ramp-up. This reduces costs during off-hours while ensuring capacity during peak.
Switch to DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode for all traffic patterns.
Reduce provisioned capacity to 500 WCU and accept throttling during peak hours.
Purchase DynamoDB reserved capacity for 5,000 WCU for cost savings.

explanation: Auto Scaling with scheduled actions provides the best cost optimization for predictable traffic patterns. Minimum capacity of 500 WCU covers overnight traffic. Scheduled pre-scaling at 7:45 AM ensures capacity is ready before peak. Target utilization of 70% allows headroom for traffic bursts. This reduces overnight costs by 90% compared to static provisioning. Option B (on-demand) is more expensive than auto-scaled provisioned capacity for predictable workloads. Option C (low provisioning) causes throttling. Option D (reserved capacity at 5K) still wastes capacity overnight.

stem: A company is migrating a high-performance computing (HPC) workload to AWS. The workload requires tight coupling between 1,000 compute nodes with low-latency, high-bandwidth MPI (Message Passing Interface) communication. The compute jobs run for 2-6 hours and are submitted to a job scheduler. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use AWS ParallelCluster to deploy and manage the HPC cluster. Configure EC2 hpc7g or hpc6a instances with Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) for low-latency MPI communication. Use Slurm as the job scheduler integrated with ParallelCluster. Store shared data on Amazon FSx for Lustre for high-throughput parallel file access. Configure compute nodes to scale dynamically based on the job queue depth.
Deploy 1,000 EC2 instances in a spread placement group for reliability.
Use AWS Batch with Fargate for HPC job scheduling and execution.
Deploy the HPC workload on Amazon EKS with 1,000 pods.

explanation: ParallelCluster provides managed HPC cluster deployment with Slurm integration. EFA on HPC-optimized instances provides the lowest latency MPI communication. FSx for Lustre provides the high-throughput parallel file system needed for HPC. Dynamic scaling based on job queue optimizes cost. Option B (spread placement group) maximizes reliability but not performance (cluster placement group is needed for low latency). Option C (Fargate) does not support EFA or MPI. Option D (EKS) adds Kubernetes overhead without HPC-specific optimizations.

stem: A company needs to implement a blockchain-based supply chain tracking system that records the provenance of products from manufacturer to consumer. The system must support smart contracts for automated compliance checks, handle 1,000 transactions per second, and integrate with existing enterprise systems. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon Managed Blockchain with Hyperledger Fabric for the permissioned blockchain network. Deploy smart contracts (chaincode) for automated compliance verification at each supply chain checkpoint. Use Amazon QLDB (Quantum Ledger Database) for an immutable transaction log that provides cryptographic verification of the complete supply chain history. Integrate with enterprise systems through Amazon API Gateway and Lambda functions that submit transactions to the blockchain network.
Build a custom blockchain implementation on EC2 instances using open-source blockchain software.
Use Amazon DynamoDB with immutable records for supply chain tracking.
Deploy Ethereum public blockchain nodes on EC2 for supply chain transactions.

explanation: Managed Blockchain with Hyperledger Fabric provides a permissioned blockchain suitable for enterprise supply chains with smart contract support. QLDB provides cryptographically verifiable, immutable ledger for compliance. API Gateway and Lambda enable integration with existing systems. Hyperledger Fabric handles 1,000 TPS. Option B (custom blockchain) requires significant development and operational expertise. Option C (DynamoDB) does not provide blockchain guarantees or smart contracts. Option D (Ethereum public) is permissionless, slower, and incurs gas costs.

stem: A company needs to implement network segmentation for PCI DSS compliance in their AWS environment. The cardholder data environment (CDE) must be isolated from non-CDE workloads. Only specific services (payment processing) should be in the CDE, and network traffic between CDE and non-CDE must be tightly controlled and logged. Which architecture should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Deploy the CDE in a dedicated VPC in a separate AWS account within a PCI-specific OU. Use AWS Transit Gateway with dedicated route tables to control traffic flow between the CDE VPC and non-CDE VPCs. Deploy AWS Network Firewall in the CDE VPC to inspect all ingress and egress traffic. Enable VPC Flow Logs with S3 delivery for all CDE traffic. Use AWS PrivateLink for any necessary communication between CDE and non-CDE services to avoid exposing services over the network.
Use security groups to separate CDE and non-CDE resources within the same VPC.
Deploy CDE resources in private subnets and non-CDE in public subnets of the same VPC.
Use NACLs to restrict traffic between CDE and non-CDE subnets in a single VPC.

explanation: Dedicated VPC in a separate account provides the strongest network segmentation for PCI CDE. Transit Gateway with dedicated route tables controls inter-VPC traffic. Network Firewall provides deep packet inspection. VPC Flow Logs provide the audit trail required by PCI DSS. PrivateLink enables secure service communication without network exposure. Option B (security groups) does not provide sufficient network segmentation for PCI. Option C (subnet separation) is insufficient isolation. Option D (NACLs) provide basic filtering but not the level of control and inspection required.

stem: A company runs a microservices application on Amazon ECS. Deployments occasionally cause outages because new task definitions contain bugs that are not caught until production. The current deployment process uses the rolling update deployment type which replaces all tasks with the new version. How should the solutions architect improve deployment safety?

options.text: Switch from rolling updates to ECS blue/green deployments using AWS CodeDeploy. Configure CodeDeploy to use a canary deployment configuration (e.g., CodeDeployDefault.ECSCanary10Percent5Minutes) that routes 10% of traffic to the new version initially. Monitor CloudWatch alarms for error rates and latency during the canary phase. Configure automatic rollback if alarms trigger. After successful canary validation, shift remaining traffic to the new version.
Add more unit tests to catch all bugs before deployment.
Deploy to a staging environment first and manually test before production.
Increase the minimum healthy percent in the rolling update to 100%.

explanation: Blue/green with canary deployment limits blast radius by initially routing only 10% of traffic to the new version. CloudWatch alarm-based automatic rollback quickly reverts if the canary shows errors. This catches production-specific bugs with minimal user impact. Option B (more unit tests) cannot catch all production issues (configuration, data, scale). Option C (staging) does not replicate production traffic patterns. Option D (100% minimum healthy) prevents deployment failures but does not validate the new version with real traffic.

stem: A company is migrating a legacy application that stores session data and user preferences in cookies (up to 8 KB per user). The cookie size is causing performance issues on mobile devices and exceeding some browser limits. During migration to AWS, the architect wants to modernize the session management. Which approach should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Replace cookie-based storage with Amazon ElastiCache for Redis. Store only a session ID in a small cookie. Keep all session data and user preferences in Redis, keyed by the session ID. Implement Redis with cluster mode enabled for high availability and automatic failover. Set TTL on Redis keys matching the session timeout. This reduces cookie size to under 100 bytes while improving performance.
Compress the cookie data to reduce its size.
Store session data in Amazon S3 and reference the S3 object key in the cookie.
Move session data to local storage on the client side using JavaScript.

explanation: Externalizing session data to Redis eliminates cookie bloat by storing only a small session ID in the cookie. Redis provides microsecond latency for session data access. Cluster mode ensures high availability. TTL automatically cleans up expired sessions. This is the industry-standard pattern for server-side session management. Option B (compression) provides limited reduction and adds processing overhead. Option C (S3) has too much latency for session data. Option D (local storage) exposes session data to client-side manipulation.

stem: A company needs to build a platform for managing and executing A/B tests across their web and mobile applications. The platform must support feature flags, traffic splitting by percentage, user segmentation, and real-time metrics collection for statistical significance testing. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon CloudWatch Evidently for feature flags and A/B test management. Evidently provides traffic splitting by percentage, user segmentation using entity overrides, and built-in statistical analysis for determining experiment winners. Integrate Evidently SDK in web and mobile applications to evaluate feature variations. Use CloudWatch metrics for real-time experiment monitoring and Evidently's built-in Bayesian analysis for statistical significance.
Build a custom A/B testing framework using Lambda functions and DynamoDB for flag storage.
Use Amazon API Gateway canary deployments for all A/B tests.
Implement client-side randomization using JavaScript and track results manually.

explanation: CloudWatch Evidently provides managed A/B testing with feature flags, percentage-based traffic splitting, user segmentation, and built-in statistical analysis. The SDK integrates directly with applications. Bayesian analysis determines statistical significance automatically. Option B (custom framework) requires building and maintaining statistical analysis, flag evaluation, and traffic splitting from scratch. Option C (API Gateway canary) is for deployment, not A/B testing features. Option D (client-side randomization) lacks server-side control and statistical rigor.

stem: A company needs to establish a secure bastion host architecture for accessing private resources across 100 AWS accounts. Traditional SSH bastion hosts create security risks with key management and open ports. The company wants a keyless, auditable solution. Which architecture should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Deploy AWS Systems Manager Session Manager as the bastion replacement. Session Manager provides browser-based and CLI shell access to EC2 instances without opening inbound ports (no SSH/RDP ports needed). All sessions are logged to CloudWatch Logs and S3 for audit. Use IAM policies to control who can start sessions to which instances. Enable Session Manager Run As to enforce specific OS-level user access. Configure KMS encryption for session data in transit.
Deploy a centralized EC2 bastion host with SSH keys managed in AWS Secrets Manager.
Use AWS Client VPN to provide direct access to private resources.
Open SSH port 22 on all instances with security groups restricted to corporate IP ranges.

explanation: Session Manager eliminates bastion hosts entirely. No inbound ports are needed (uses SSM agent outbound HTTPS). IAM controls access at the user-to-instance level. All sessions are encrypted with KMS and fully logged for audit. Run As enforces OS-level user mapping. This is keyless (no SSH keys to manage). Option B (bastion with keys) still requires key management and open ports. Option C (Client VPN) provides network access but not session auditing. Option D (open SSH) creates a larger attack surface.

stem: A company operates an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL cluster that serves both a web application (short transactional queries) and a reporting tool (long-running analytical queries). The reporting queries are degrading web application performance by consuming shared resources. The company cannot afford to run a separate analytics database. How should the solutions architect resolve this without additional database costs?

options.text: Create an Aurora replica (reader instance) and direct all reporting queries to the reader endpoint. Configure the web application to use the writer endpoint exclusively. The Aurora replica shares the same storage volume as the writer (no additional storage cost) and only incurs compute cost for the reader instance, which is cheaper than a separate analytics database. Use connection pooling with PgBouncer to efficiently manage connections on both endpoints.
Increase the writer instance class to handle both workloads.
Move reporting queries to run only between midnight and 6 AM.
Create materialized views for all report queries to reduce execution time.

explanation: Aurora read replicas share the same storage cluster (no storage duplication cost). Separating read and write workloads eliminates resource contention. The reader instance handles analytical queries without affecting the writer's performance for transactional queries. PgBouncer optimizes connection usage. Option B (bigger instance) adds cost without separation. Option C (scheduling) limits reporting availability. Option D (materialized views) may help but does not solve the fundamental resource contention.

stem: A company is migrating a large-scale ETL pipeline from on-premises Apache Spark clusters to AWS. The pipeline processes 5 TB of data daily from various sources, performs complex transformations, and loads results into a data warehouse. The company wants to reduce operational overhead while maintaining Spark compatibility. Which migration approach should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Migrate Spark jobs to AWS Glue with Spark ETL. Use AWS Glue jobs with Spark-compatible PySpark or Scala code, requiring minimal code changes. Enable Glue auto-scaling to optimize worker allocation. Use Glue job bookmarks for incremental processing. Store intermediate data in S3 with Parquet format. Use Glue workflows to orchestrate the pipeline. Load results into Amazon Redshift using the Glue Redshift connector with COPY optimization.
Deploy Amazon EMR clusters running 24/7 with the same Spark configuration as on-premises.
Rewrite all Spark jobs as AWS Lambda functions.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics for all ETL processing.

explanation: Glue provides serverless Spark with minimal code changes from existing PySpark/Scala. Auto-scaling eliminates capacity management. Job bookmarks enable incremental processing (only process new data). Glue workflows provide managed orchestration. The Redshift connector optimizes data loading. Option B (24/7 EMR) requires cluster management and wastes resources during idle periods. Option C (Lambda) cannot handle Spark-level data processing. Option D (Kinesis Analytics) is for stream processing, not batch ETL.

stem: A company is building a platform for processing insurance claims using document understanding. The platform must extract data from various document types (claim forms, medical records, invoices, photos of damage), verify the extracted data against policy terms, and flag suspicious claims for fraud investigation. Which TWO services should the solutions architect include? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Use Amazon Textract for extracting structured data from claim forms and invoices (tables, key-value pairs, signatures). Use Amazon Comprehend Medical for extracting medical entities (diagnoses, medications, procedures) from medical records.

Use Amazon Bedrock with a foundation model to build a claims processing agent that can reason about extracted data, verify against policy terms, and identify fraud patterns using chain-of-thought analysis across multiple data sources.
Use Amazon Translate to convert all documents to English before processing.
Use Amazon Polly to read document contents aloud for human reviewers.
Use Amazon Lex to build a chatbot for claims submission.

explanation: Textract extracts structured data from forms and invoices. Comprehend Medical extracts medical entities from clinical documents. Together (Option A) they handle all document types. Bedrock (Option B) provides reasoning capabilities to verify extracted data against policy terms and identify fraud patterns using AI analysis across multiple data points. Option C (Translate) is only needed for multi-language documents. Option D (Polly) does not help with automated processing. Option E (Lex chatbot) is for conversational interfaces, not document processing.

stem: A company must implement a strategy for managing AWS account root user credentials across 300 accounts in their AWS Organization. The security team requires that root users have MFA enabled, root access keys are deleted, and root login events trigger immediate alerts. Which approach should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Use AWS Organizations centralized root access management to remove root credentials from member accounts entirely. For the management account, enable a hardware MFA device and store the MFA device and root password in a physical safe with dual-control access procedures. Create AWS Config rules that check for root access key existence across all accounts. Create an EventBridge rule that matches ConsoleLogin events with userIdentity.type of Root and triggers an SNS notification to the security team for immediate investigation.
Share the root password across the security team for emergency access.
Create IAM users named root-backup in each account as an alternative to root.
Disable root access entirely across all accounts with no recovery mechanism.

explanation: Centralized root access management in Organizations removes the need for root credentials in member accounts. Hardware MFA with physical safe and dual-control provides the most secure root access for the management account. Config rules provide continuous compliance checking for access keys. EventBridge rules provide real-time alerting for root login attempts. Option B (shared password) violates security best practices. Option C (IAM root-backup) does not have root-level access. Option D (no recovery) creates risk of account lockout.

stem: A company uses AWS Lambda functions extensively. The Lambda functions share common dependencies (SDK libraries, utility functions, data access layers) that are duplicated across 50 Lambda functions. When a shared library needs updating, the team must modify and redeploy all 50 functions. How should the solutions architect reduce this duplication and operational burden?

options.text: Create AWS Lambda Layers for shared dependencies. Package common SDK libraries, utility functions, and data access layers as separate Lambda Layers. Reference these Layers in all 50 Lambda functions. When a shared library needs updating, update only the Layer version and configure functions to use the new Layer version. Use Lambda aliases with weighted routing to gradually roll out Layer updates across functions.
Consolidate all 50 Lambda functions into a single monolithic function.
Move shared code to a private npm/PyPI package and rebuild all functions when it changes.
Copy shared code into an S3 bucket and download it at function runtime.

explanation: Lambda Layers provide a mechanism to share code and libraries across multiple functions. Updating a Layer version requires redeploying only the Layer, not all 50 functions. Functions can be configured to use the new Layer version gradually using aliases with weighted routing. This reduces duplication and simplifies updates. Option B (monolithic function) loses the benefits of separate functions. Option C (package registry) still requires rebuilding and redeploying all functions. Option D (S3 download) adds latency to every cold start.

stem: A company is migrating from a commercial API gateway (Apigee/MuleSoft) to AWS. The existing gateway handles API versioning, request/response transformation, rate limiting, API key management, and developer portal functionality. Which AWS service and configuration should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon API Gateway REST API with stages for API versioning (v1, v2). Configure mapping templates (VTL) for request/response transformation. Implement usage plans with API keys for rate limiting and throttling per customer. Deploy the API Gateway Developer Portal (Serverless Application Repository) for API documentation and developer self-service. Use API Gateway resource policies for IP-based access control.
Use an Application Load Balancer with path-based routing for API management.
Deploy Kong API Gateway on Amazon EKS for a self-managed solution.
Use Amazon CloudFront with Lambda@Edge for API management functions.

explanation: API Gateway REST API provides all the enterprise API management features: stages for versioning, VTL mapping templates for transformation, usage plans with API keys for rate limiting, and the Developer Portal for self-service documentation. Resource policies provide IP-based access control. This replaces commercial API gateway functionality with a managed AWS service. Option B (ALB) lacks API management features. Option C (Kong on EKS) requires infrastructure management. Option D (CloudFront/Lambda@Edge) is not designed for full API management.

stem: A company needs to build a natural language processing (NLP) pipeline that processes customer reviews in 12 languages. The pipeline must detect sentiment, extract key phrases, identify the language, and categorize reviews by topic. The company processes 1 million reviews daily. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon Comprehend for the complete NLP pipeline. Comprehend provides built-in language detection, sentiment analysis, key phrase extraction, and topic modeling across 12+ languages. Process reviews in batches using Comprehend's asynchronous batch operations for cost efficiency at 1M reviews/day. Store results in Amazon OpenSearch for searchable analysis and Amazon S3 for long-term storage. Orchestrate the pipeline with Step Functions.
Build custom NLP models using Amazon SageMaker for each of the 12 languages.
Use Amazon Translate to convert all reviews to English, then process with a single-language NLP model.
Deploy open-source NLP libraries (spaCy, NLTK) on EC2 instances for text processing.

explanation: Comprehend provides managed, multi-language NLP with all required capabilities (sentiment, key phrases, language detection, topic modeling) out of the box. Batch operations optimize cost for high-volume processing. No custom model training is needed. Option B (12 custom SageMaker models) requires significant ML expertise and maintenance per language. Option C (translate first) adds cost and may lose nuance in translation. Option D (self-managed NLP) requires infrastructure management and model maintenance.

stem: A company has deployed AWS Outposts in a factory for low-latency local processing of manufacturing data. The Outposts rack processes IoT sensor data locally for real-time quality control decisions. The company needs to ensure data is synchronized with the AWS Region for long-term analytics while maintaining operations during network disconnections from the Region. Which architecture should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Process real-time quality control data using Amazon ECS on Outposts with local data storage on Amazon EBS local volumes. Use Amazon S3 on Outposts for local object storage during network disconnections. Configure S3 on Outposts to replicate data to the Region-based S3 bucket when connectivity is restored using S3 access points. Deploy AWS IoT Greengrass on Outposts for local IoT device management that operates independently during disconnections.
Use AWS Direct Connect as the sole mechanism to ensure uninterrupted connectivity.
Store all data in the AWS Region and use caching on Outposts for frequently accessed data.
Deploy a complete standalone system on Outposts with no Region dependency.

explanation: S3 on Outposts provides local storage that operates during disconnections and syncs to the Region when connected. ECS on Outposts runs containers locally for real-time processing. IoT Greengrass enables local IoT operations independent of Region connectivity. EBS local volumes provide block storage for databases. Option B (Direct Connect) can still fail; the architecture must handle disconnections. Option C (Region storage with cache) fails during disconnections. Option D (standalone) loses the benefit of Region analytics and cloud services.

stem: A company has a CI/CD pipeline that deploys Lambda functions using AWS SAM. The deployment process takes 15 minutes because it packages and uploads all function code even when only one function changes. The SAM template defines 30 Lambda functions with shared layers. How should the solutions architect optimize the deployment time?

options.text: Implement AWS SAM Accelerate (sam sync) for development deployments, which detects changes and only updates modified functions. For production, split the single SAM template into multiple nested stacks grouped by business domain, allowing independent deployment of each stack. Use SAM build with the --cached flag to skip rebuilding unchanged functions. Configure CodePipeline with parallel deployment stages for independent stacks.
Increase the CodeBuild instance size to speed up packaging.
Deploy all functions manually through the AWS Console to save time.
Remove Lambda Layers and inline all dependencies in each function.

explanation: SAM Accelerate detects changes and only deploys modified functions, reducing iteration time from 15 minutes to seconds during development. Nested stacks enable independent deployment of related functions. Cached builds skip unchanged functions. Parallel pipeline stages deploy independent stacks simultaneously. Option B (bigger CodeBuild) slightly speeds up packaging but does not eliminate unnecessary repackaging. Option C (manual deployment) is error-prone and not repeatable. Option D (removing Layers) increases duplication and package sizes.

stem: A company is migrating a legacy application that uses FTP for file transfers with external partners. The company receives 500 files daily from 50 partners. Each partner has unique FTP credentials. The company wants to eliminate managing FTP server infrastructure while maintaining partner compatibility. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use AWS Transfer Family with the SFTP, FTPS, and FTP protocols enabled. Configure Transfer Family with Amazon S3 as the storage backend. Create per-partner users with scoped-down IAM roles that restrict access to partner-specific S3 prefixes. Use custom identity providers backed by Lambda and DynamoDB for partner authentication. Configure S3 event notifications to trigger processing workflows when files arrive.
Deploy an FTP server on an EC2 instance with EBS storage.
Replace FTP with Amazon API Gateway REST APIs for file uploads.
Use Amazon WorkDocs for file sharing with external partners.

explanation: Transfer Family provides fully managed SFTP/FTPS/FTP servers compatible with existing partner FTP clients (no partner-side changes). S3 backend provides durable, scalable storage. Per-partner scoped-down roles provide security isolation. Custom identity providers integrate with existing partner credential management. S3 events trigger automated processing. Option B (EC2 FTP) requires infrastructure management. Option C (API Gateway) requires partners to change their integration. Option D (WorkDocs) is not designed for automated file transfers.

stem: A company is building a platform for running regulatory compliance simulations for financial institutions. Each simulation requires running millions of Monte Carlo iterations using proprietary risk models. Simulations are run quarterly and each takes 4-8 hours on 10,000 vCPUs. The platform is idle between quarterly runs. Which architecture maximizes cost efficiency?

options.text: Use AWS Batch with Spot Instances for compute. Configure Batch compute environments with multiple instance types across multiple Availability Zones for maximum Spot capacity. Use Spot Fleet allocation strategies with capacity-optimized to minimize interruptions. Implement checkpointing in the simulation code to save progress to S3, allowing interrupted simulations to resume rather than restart. Use AWS Step Functions to orchestrate the simulation workflow with retry logic for Spot interruptions.
Purchase Reserved Instances for 10,000 vCPUs to ensure availability.
Use On-Demand instances for all simulation compute.
Run simulations on AWS Lambda with maximum concurrency.

explanation: Spot Instances provide up to 90% cost savings for fault-tolerant workloads like Monte Carlo simulations. Capacity-optimized allocation minimizes interruptions. Checkpointing to S3 enables resume-on-interrupt, preventing lost computation. Batch manages job scheduling across thousands of instances. Step Functions orchestrates the workflow. The platform costs near-zero between quarterly runs. Option B (Reserved Instances) wastes money when idle between quarters. Option C (On-Demand) costs 5-10x more than Spot. Option D (Lambda) has 15-minute timeout and limited CPU.

stem: A company needs to implement a multi-account strategy for a new AWS environment. The company has 4 business units, each with development, staging, and production workloads. A central platform team manages shared infrastructure. Security and compliance requirements mandate separation of duties. Which AWS Organizations structure should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Create an OU structure with: Root OU containing Security OU (log archive, security tooling accounts), Infrastructure OU (networking, shared services accounts), and a Workloads OU with child OUs per business unit (each containing Dev, Staging, Prod accounts). Apply SCPs at each OU level: deny Regions outside approved list at Root, deny destructive actions in Production OUs, allow broader permissions in Dev OUs. Use AWS Control Tower for automated account provisioning and guardrails.
Create a flat structure with all accounts directly under the root OU.
Create one AWS account per business unit with separate VPCs for each environment.
Create separate Organizations for each business unit.

explanation: Hierarchical OU structure enables tiered governance: Root-level SCPs enforce organization-wide constraints, OU-level SCPs enforce environment-specific policies (e.g., stricter production controls). Separation of security, infrastructure, and workload accounts follows AWS best practices. Control Tower automates account provisioning with consistent guardrails. Option B (flat structure) cannot apply differentiated policies. Option C (single account per BU) mixes environments. Option D (separate Organizations) prevents centralized governance.

stem: A company's application processes files uploaded to Amazon S3. Each file triggers a Lambda function that processes and writes results to DynamoDB. During peak hours, the system processes 10,000 files per minute. The company notices that some DynamoDB writes fail with ProvisionedThroughputExceededException despite having adequate overall capacity. Investigation shows that all writes target a single partition because files are processed in alphabetical order and the DynamoDB partition key is the file path. How should the solutions architect fix this?

options.text: Redesign the DynamoDB partition key to use a high-cardinality attribute such as a UUID or a hash of the file path. This ensures writes are distributed evenly across all DynamoDB partitions. If the file path must remain queryable, add it as a Global Secondary Index. Alternatively, use a composite partition key combining a random prefix (1-10) with the file path, and use scatter-gather reads to query all partitions.
Increase the provisioned WCU on the DynamoDB table.
Enable DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode.
Add a DAX cluster in front of DynamoDB for write buffering.

explanation: The hot partition problem occurs because sequential file paths map to the same partition. High-cardinality keys (UUID, hash) distribute writes evenly. GSI enables querying by the original file path. Write sharding with random prefixes is an alternative distribution strategy. Option B (more WCU) does not solve hot partitions since capacity is distributed evenly. Option C (on-demand) still has per-partition throughput limits. Option D (DAX) is a read cache, not a write buffer.

stem: A company is migrating a .NET application that uses Windows Task Scheduler for running 200 scheduled jobs. The jobs include database maintenance scripts, report generation, file processing, and data synchronization tasks. Jobs run at various intervals (every 5 minutes to monthly). The company wants a managed scheduling solution on AWS. Which approach should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon EventBridge Scheduler for all scheduled job execution. Create individual schedules with cron or rate expressions matching the existing Windows Task Scheduler intervals. Configure EventBridge Scheduler to invoke appropriate targets: Lambda functions for lightweight jobs, ECS Fargate tasks for compute-intensive jobs, and Step Functions for multi-step workflows. Use dead-letter queues for failed invocations and retry policies for transient failures.
Deploy Windows Task Scheduler on an EC2 Windows instance.
Use CloudWatch Events rules for all 200 scheduled jobs.
Create 200 Lambda functions with self-scheduling using CloudWatch Events.

explanation: EventBridge Scheduler provides at-rest scheduling (one-time and recurring) with built-in retry policies, DLQs, and flexible targeting. It supports various targets (Lambda, ECS, Step Functions) matching the diverse job requirements. Cron and rate expressions match Windows Task Scheduler patterns. Option B (EC2 Windows) replicates the on-premises pattern without modernization. Option C (CloudWatch Events) is being superseded by EventBridge and lacks scheduling-specific features like DLQs. Option D (self-scheduling Lambda) is over-engineered.

stem: A company is building a platform for real-time language translation of live customer support calls. The platform must transcribe audio from customers speaking various languages, translate the transcription to the agent's language in real time, and provide the translated text on the agent's screen within 2 seconds. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon Transcribe Streaming for real-time speech-to-text with automatic language identification. Pipe the transcription output to Amazon Translate for real-time text translation. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams as the intermediate buffer between transcription and translation. Deliver translated text to the agent's interface through Amazon API Gateway WebSocket APIs for real-time push delivery. Store conversation transcripts in Amazon S3 for compliance and quality review.
Record the entire call first, then process with batch transcription and translation.
Use Amazon Polly to generate translated audio for the agent instead of text.
Build a custom speech recognition model using SageMaker for each language.

explanation: Transcribe Streaming provides real-time speech-to-text with automatic language detection. Translate provides real-time text translation between language pairs. Kinesis buffers and streams between services. API Gateway WebSocket delivers translated text to the agent's screen in real time. S3 stores transcripts for compliance. Option B (batch processing) does not meet the 2-second requirement. Option C (Polly audio) adds text-to-speech overhead; agents can read faster than listening. Option D (custom models per language) requires massive ML investment.

stem: A company operates a hybrid environment with workloads in AWS and Azure. The company needs to implement a unified identity solution that allows employees to access resources in both clouds using a single set of credentials. The company uses Azure AD as their primary identity provider. Which solution should the solutions architect implement for the AWS side?

options.text: Configure AWS IAM Identity Center with Azure AD as the external SAML 2.0 identity provider. Enable automatic user provisioning using SCIM from Azure AD to IAM Identity Center. Map Azure AD groups to IAM Identity Center permission sets for role-based access. Configure session duration limits. Users authenticate through Azure AD's SSO portal and are federated into AWS accounts with appropriate permissions based on their Azure AD group membership.
Create matching IAM users in AWS for each Azure AD user.
Use AWS Directory Service Managed Microsoft AD as the primary identity provider for both clouds.
Install Azure AD Connect on an EC2 instance to sync identities to AWS.

explanation: IAM Identity Center with Azure AD SAML federation provides seamless SSO for employees using their Azure AD credentials. SCIM auto-provisioning keeps AWS user records synchronized with Azure AD. Group-to-permission-set mapping enables consistent RBAC. Users experience single sign-on across both clouds. Option B (matching IAM users) requires manual synchronization and separate credentials. Option C (Managed AD) adds an unnecessary directory service. Option D (Azure AD Connect) is designed for Azure AD to on-premises AD sync, not AWS.

stem: A company runs an application that writes 100,000 small objects (1-10 KB each) per second to Amazon S3. The application is experiencing high latency on PUT operations. The objects are written with sequential keys (timestamp-based) like 2024/01/15/12:00:00/object-001. How should the solutions architect improve write performance?

options.text: Add a random hash prefix to the S3 object keys to distribute writes across multiple S3 partitions. For example, change keys from '2024/01/15/object-001' to 'a3f2/2024/01/15/object-001' where 'a3f2' is a hex hash. This prevents sequential key writes from concentrating on a single S3 partition, which can throttle at the partition level. Maintain a mapping or use deterministic hashing for key reconstruction during reads.
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration for all PUT operations.
Switch to S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class for better performance.
Increase the number of concurrent PUT connections to S3.

explanation: S3 partitions data by key prefix. Sequential, timestamp-based keys concentrate writes on a single partition, causing throttling. Adding a random hash prefix distributes writes across multiple partitions, enabling S3 to achieve its full throughput capability (3,500 PUT/sec per prefix). Note: as of 2023, S3 auto-partitions better, but for 100K writes/sec, explicit key randomization ensures optimal distribution. Option B (Transfer Acceleration) improves long-distance transfer, not local write throughput. Option C (storage class) does not affect write performance. Option D (more connections) helps but does not solve the partition bottleneck.

stem: A company is modernizing a legacy monolithic application by extracting a payment processing module as the first microservice. The payment module handles credit card processing, refunds, and payment reconciliation. During the extraction, both the monolith and the new microservice must be able to process payments without data inconsistency. Which approach should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Implement the Branch by Abstraction pattern: create a payment abstraction layer within the monolith. Initially, the abstraction delegates to the existing monolith code. Gradually implement the new payment microservice on Amazon ECS behind the abstraction. Use feature flags (AWS AppConfig) to route payment requests between the monolith implementation and the new microservice. Both implementations write to the same database during the transition. Once validated, remove the monolith implementation and switch fully to the microservice.
Run both systems simultaneously processing all payments and reconcile differences daily.
Stop the monolith entirely and deploy the new microservice immediately.
Copy all payment data to a new database for the microservice and keep both databases synchronized indefinitely.

explanation: Branch by Abstraction enables incremental extraction with a safety net. The abstraction layer provides a single interface while routing between implementations. Feature flags (AppConfig) enable gradual, reversible traffic shifting. Sharing the same database during transition prevents data inconsistency. This is lower risk than any big-bang approach. Option B (dual processing) creates inconsistency and double charges. Option C (stop monolith) is high-risk big-bang. Option D (synchronized databases) adds complexity and eventual consistency challenges.

stem: A company needs to build an anomaly detection system for their e-commerce platform. The system must detect unusual patterns in transaction volumes, cart abandonment rates, and page response times. Anomalies should trigger automated investigation workflows. The company does not have data science expertise. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon Lookout for Metrics to automatically detect anomalies in business metrics without ML expertise. Connect Lookout for Metrics to Amazon CloudWatch, Amazon S3, Amazon RDS, and Amazon Redshift as data sources. Configure metric dimensions (product category, region, device type) for root cause analysis. Integrate with AWS Lambda via Amazon SNS notifications to trigger automated investigation workflows when anomalies are detected. Lookout for Metrics uses ML to learn normal patterns and identify deviations.
Build custom anomaly detection models using Amazon SageMaker.
Set static threshold alarms in Amazon CloudWatch for all metrics.
Hire a data science team to develop and maintain anomaly detection algorithms.

explanation: Lookout for Metrics provides no-code anomaly detection using ML that learns normal metric patterns automatically. It connects to multiple data sources without ETL. Severity ranking and dimensional root cause analysis help identify the source of anomalies. SNS integration enables automated workflows. No ML expertise is needed. Option B (SageMaker) requires data science expertise the company lacks. Option C (static thresholds) cannot adapt to seasonal patterns and generates false alarms. Option D (hiring) is expensive and time-consuming.

stem: A company needs to implement a service control policy (SCP) strategy that prevents developers from disabling security services (GuardDuty, Security Hub, Config, CloudTrail) while still allowing the security team to manage these services. How should the solutions architect implement this differentiated access?

options.text: Create an SCP that denies actions like guardduty:DeleteDetector, securityhub:DisableSecurityHub, config:StopConfigurationRecorder, and cloudtrail:StopLogging. Add a condition to the SCP that exempts a specific IAM role (SecurityAdminRole) used exclusively by the security team. Attach this SCP to all OUs containing workload accounts. The security team assumes the SecurityAdminRole through IAM Identity Center to manage security services, while all other roles are blocked from disabling them.
Give the security team root access to manage security services.
Create separate accounts for the security team that are not subject to SCPs.
Use IAM policies instead of SCPs to control access to security services.

explanation: SCPs with role-based exemptions provide organization-wide preventive controls while allowing the security team to perform their duties. The condition key aws:PrincipalArn exempts the security role from the deny policy. SCPs cannot be overridden by account-level IAM policies, ensuring protection. The security role is tightly controlled through IAM Identity Center. Option B (root access) is a security risk. Option C (exempt accounts) does not apply SCPs to those accounts at all. Option D (IAM policies) can be overridden by account administrators.

stem: A company uses Amazon EKS with the AWS Load Balancer Controller. The application requires WebSocket connections that persist for up to 24 hours. Users report frequent WebSocket disconnections. Investigation shows that the ALB idle timeout (60 seconds default) is closing connections when no messages are exchanged for more than 60 seconds. How should the solutions architect resolve this?

options.text: Increase the ALB idle timeout to the maximum value (4000 seconds). Implement application-level WebSocket ping/pong heartbeat frames at 30-second intervals to keep the connection active during periods without application messages. The heartbeat ensures the connection never appears idle to the ALB, preventing timeout-based disconnections even during quiet periods that exceed the idle timeout.

Switch from ALB to a Network Load Balancer, which supports unlimited idle timeout for TCP connections and does not terminate WebSocket connections. Configure the NLB target group with a TCP health check. This is the optimal solution for long-lived WebSocket connections.
Deploy a separate WebSocket server on EC2 instances without a load balancer.
Use Amazon API Gateway WebSocket APIs instead of ALB for WebSocket connections.

explanation: NLB operates at Layer 4 (TCP) and does not have an idle timeout for TCP connections, making it ideal for long-lived WebSocket connections that may be idle for extended periods. NLB passes WebSocket traffic through without protocol-level interpretation. ALB (Option A) has a maximum idle timeout of 4000 seconds (~67 minutes), insufficient for 24-hour connections even with heartbeats during truly silent periods. Option C (no LB) loses high availability. Option D (API Gateway WebSocket) has a 2-hour maximum connection duration.

stem: A company is migrating a large on-premises PostgreSQL database (20 TB) to Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL. The application cannot tolerate more than 1 hour of downtime. The on-premises network has a 1 Gbps Direct Connect connection to AWS. At 1 Gbps, transferring 20 TB would take approximately 44 hours. How should the solutions architect minimize downtime?

options.text: Use AWS DMS with a full load followed by ongoing CDC (Change Data Capture) replication. Start the full load migration days before the cutover window. DMS uses the Direct Connect link to transfer the initial 20 TB while the source database remains operational. Once the full load is complete, DMS CDC keeps the Aurora target synchronized with ongoing changes. During the 1-hour cutover window, stop application writes, let DMS catch up on remaining changes, validate data, and switch the application to Aurora.
Use pg_dump and pg_restore to export and import the entire database during the maintenance window.
Use AWS Snowball Edge to physically ship the data to AWS.
Increase the Direct Connect connection to 10 Gbps before migration.

explanation: DMS with full load + CDC enables near-zero downtime migration. The full load transfers the 20 TB over days while the application runs normally. CDC captures ongoing changes during the full load transfer. The final cutover only requires catching up on the remaining CDC lag, which takes minutes, well within the 1-hour window. Option B (pg_dump/restore) requires 44+ hours of downtime. Option C (Snowball) adds days for shipping and does not handle ongoing changes. Option D (10 Gbps upgrade) still takes 4.4 hours for a single transfer.

stem: A company needs to implement a secrets rotation strategy for database credentials used by 50 Lambda functions. The credentials must be rotated every 30 days without application downtime. The Lambda functions connect to Amazon Aurora MySQL. Which architecture should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Store database credentials in AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation enabled. Configure Secrets Manager rotation Lambda function to use the alternating users rotation strategy, which creates two sets of credentials and alternates between them during rotation (ensuring one set is always valid).
