Configure all 50 Lambda functions to retrieve credentials from Secrets Manager at runtime using the AWS SDK with caching. Use Secrets Manager VPC endpoint for private access from Lambda functions in VPCs.
Store credentials in environment variables of each Lambda function and update them monthly.
Store credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store with no rotation mechanism.
Hard-code credentials in the Lambda function source code with manual updates.

explanation: Secrets Manager with alternating users rotation ensures zero downtime during rotation by maintaining two valid credential sets. The rotation Lambda function updates credentials in the database and Secrets Manager atomically. Lambda functions retrieve credentials at runtime (with SDK caching for performance). VPC endpoint provides private, low-latency access. Option B (environment variables) requires redeploying all 50 functions. Option C (Parameter Store) does not have built-in rotation. Option D (hard-coded) is a security anti-pattern.

stem: A company operates in a regulated industry where all network traffic entering and leaving their AWS VPCs must be inspected by an intrusion detection/prevention system (IDS/IPS). The company has 30 VPCs across 3 Regions. The solution must support centralized rule management and logging. Which architecture should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Deploy AWS Network Firewall in a centralized inspection VPC per Region. Route all VPC traffic through Transit Gateway to the inspection VPC. Configure Network Firewall with Suricata-compatible IDS/IPS rules for threat detection and prevention. Use Network Firewall rule groups managed centrally through AWS Firewall Manager for consistent rule deployment across all 3 Regions. Send firewall logs to a centralized S3 bucket for analysis and retention.
Deploy open-source Snort IDS on EC2 instances in each VPC.
Use VPC Flow Logs with CloudWatch anomaly detection for intrusion detection.
Configure security groups as the primary IDS/IPS mechanism.

explanation: Network Firewall provides managed, Suricata-compatible IDS/IPS with deep packet inspection. Centralized inspection VPC with Transit Gateway routes all traffic through inspection. Firewall Manager enables centralized rule management across all 3 Regions and 30 VPCs. Centralized logging to S3 provides compliance evidence. Option B (Snort on EC2) requires managing 30+ IDS instances. Option C (Flow Logs) provides metadata only, not deep packet inspection. Option D (security groups) provide stateful filtering, not IDS/IPS.

stem: A company uses Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to process clickstream data. The stream has 100 shards processing 50,000 records per second. The company notices that consumer applications are falling behind (iterator age increasing) because a single Lambda consumer processes records sequentially within each shard. How should the solutions architect improve consumer throughput?

options.text: Enable Kinesis Data Streams enhanced fan-out for the consumer application. Enhanced fan-out provides a dedicated 2 MB/sec throughput per shard per consumer, eliminating contention between consumers. Additionally, configure the Lambda event source mapping with parallelization factor of 10 to process multiple batches from each shard concurrently. This increases per-shard processing parallelism from 1 to 10 concurrent Lambda invocations per shard.
Double the number of shards to 200 to increase overall stream capacity.
Increase the Lambda function timeout to process larger batches.
Switch from Lambda to EC2-based KCL consumers for faster processing.

explanation: Enhanced fan-out provides dedicated throughput per consumer, eliminating polling contention. Parallelization factor enables multiple concurrent Lambda invocations per shard, increasing processing parallelism 10x without adding shards. Together, these dramatically increase consumer throughput. Option B (more shards) increases cost and may not solve the per-shard processing bottleneck. Option C (longer timeout) does not increase parallelism. Option D (KCL on EC2) requires infrastructure management without necessarily being faster.

stem: A company is migrating an application that uses Oracle Golden Gate for real-time database replication between an OLTP database and a reporting database. The company wants to replace Oracle Golden Gate during migration to AWS. Which solution provides equivalent real-time replication capabilities?

options.text: Use AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) with ongoing replication (CDC) to continuously replicate changes from the source OLTP database (Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL) to the reporting database (Amazon Redshift). Configure DMS with the appropriate task settings for transformation rules and table mappings. For real-time analytics, use Aurora zero-ETL integration with Redshift as an alternative that eliminates the need for a separate replication tool entirely.
Use Oracle Golden Gate on Amazon EC2 instances.
Schedule nightly pg_dump/pg_restore between the databases.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for database replication.

explanation: DMS with CDC provides continuous, real-time replication equivalent to Golden Gate with support for schema transformation. Aurora zero-ETL integration with Redshift provides a native, fully managed alternative that requires no replication infrastructure. Both options eliminate Oracle Golden Gate licensing costs. Option B (Golden Gate on EC2) retains Oracle licensing costs. Option C (nightly dump) is not real-time. Option D (Kinesis) is for stream processing, not database replication.

stem: A company is building a digital twin platform for manufacturing plants. The platform must create virtual representations of physical equipment, ingest real-time sensor data to update equipment state, run simulations to predict maintenance needs, and visualize the factory floor in 3D. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use AWS IoT TwinMaker to build digital twin models of manufacturing equipment with entity-component relationships. Connect TwinMaker to AWS IoT SiteWise for industrial data ingestion and asset modeling from PLCs and SCADA systems. Use Amazon Managed Grafana for operational dashboards showing real-time equipment state. Integrate with Amazon SageMaker for predictive maintenance models that analyze sensor data patterns. Use TwinMaker's 3D scene viewer for factory floor visualization.
Build custom 3D visualization using WebGL on EC2 instances.
Store all sensor data in Amazon DynamoDB and build custom dashboards.
Use Amazon QuickSight for all visualization and analytics needs.

explanation: IoT TwinMaker provides purpose-built digital twin capabilities with entity modeling, data connectors, and 3D visualization. IoT SiteWise handles industrial data ingestion from OT systems (PLCs, SCADA). Grafana provides real-time operational dashboards. SageMaker enables predictive maintenance ML models. Together they create an end-to-end digital twin platform. Option B (custom WebGL) requires extensive development. Option C (DynamoDB) lacks digital twin and visualization capabilities. Option D (QuickSight) is not designed for 3D or real-time industrial visualization.

stem: A company needs to implement automated compliance remediation across their AWS Organization. When a resource is found to be non-compliant (e.g., S3 bucket without encryption, security group with 0.0.0.0/0 inbound rule), it must be automatically remediated within 15 minutes. The remediation must be auditable and reversible. Which solution should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Deploy AWS Config organization rules to detect non-compliant resources across all accounts. Configure Config auto-remediation using AWS Systems Manager Automation documents as remediation actions. Create custom Automation documents that enable S3 encryption, remove open security group rules, and other remediation tasks. Configure maximum automatic remediation attempts and use CloudTrail to audit all remediation actions. Store Automation execution history for reversibility verification.
Create Lambda functions triggered by CloudWatch Events to fix non-compliant resources.
Use AWS Trusted Advisor to identify and manually fix non-compliant resources.
Deploy third-party compliance tools across all accounts for automated remediation.

explanation: Config organization rules provide consistent compliance detection across all accounts. Auto-remediation with SSM Automation provides standardized, auditable remediation. Automation documents are reusable and versioned for consistency. CloudTrail provides audit trail. Execution history enables reviewing what was changed and when. Option B (custom Lambda) requires building and maintaining remediation logic per rule. Option C (Trusted Advisor) requires manual intervention. Option D (third-party tools) adds operational complexity.

stem: A company uses Amazon CloudFront to distribute a web application. The security team has identified that some API endpoints behind CloudFront are being targeted by credential stuffing attacks. The attackers use distributed IP addresses to avoid rate-limiting based on IP. How should the solutions architect protect against these attacks?

options.text: Deploy AWS WAF with CloudFront and configure an AWS WAF Bot Control managed rule group to detect and block automated credential stuffing attempts. Implement AWS WAF rate-based rules that limit login attempts per user account (using a custom request header or cookie containing the username). Create a WAF rule that challenges requests matching known attack patterns using CAPTCHA. Enable AWS WAF logging to Amazon S3 for security analysis and forensics.
Block all IP addresses that make more than 10 requests per minute.
Require all users to change their passwords immediately.
Disable the login API endpoint during detected attacks.

explanation: WAF Bot Control uses ML to detect automated bot traffic (credential stuffing) regardless of IP distribution. Account-based rate limiting (using username in custom header) prevents per-account brute force even from distributed IPs. CAPTCHA challenges suspicious requests while allowing legitimate users. WAF logging provides forensic data. Option B (IP-based blocking) is ineffective against distributed attacks. Option C (password changes) is disruptive and does not stop the attack. Option D (disabling login) causes a denial of service.

stem: A company is modernizing a monolithic e-commerce application. The first microservice to extract is the product catalog, which currently serves 10,000 requests per second. During the extraction, both the monolith and the new microservice must serve catalog data consistently. The company uses PostgreSQL for the catalog data. Which data migration strategy should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use the Database Wrapping pattern: create a thin API layer (Amazon API Gateway + Lambda) in front of the existing PostgreSQL catalog tables. Both the monolith and the new catalog microservice access data through this API layer. Gradually migrate catalog data to a dedicated DynamoDB table for the microservice using DMS CDC for synchronization. Once migration is validated, update the API layer to read from DynamoDB, and eventually retire the PostgreSQL catalog tables.
Allow both the monolith and microservice to connect directly to the same PostgreSQL database tables.
Copy catalog data to a new database immediately and manually synchronize changes.
Freeze catalog updates during the migration to prevent inconsistency.

explanation: The Database Wrapping pattern creates an abstraction layer that decouples consumers from the data store. Both the monolith and microservice access data through the API, enabling gradual backend migration. DMS CDC keeps databases synchronized during transition. The API layer can switch backends transparently. Option B (direct dual access) creates coupling and makes future migration harder. Option C (manual sync) is error-prone at 10K req/sec. Option D (freezing) is unacceptable for an e-commerce catalog.

stem: A company needs to build a video analysis platform that processes security camera footage from 1,000 cameras. The platform must detect specific objects (people, vehicles, packages), track movement patterns, and send real-time alerts when unauthorized access is detected. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon Kinesis Video Streams to ingest video from 1,000 cameras. Deploy Amazon Rekognition Video with stream processors for real-time object detection on Kinesis Video Streams. Use Rekognition custom labels for detecting specific objects relevant to the company's security requirements. Route detection events through Amazon EventBridge to trigger Lambda functions for alert processing and Amazon SNS for real-time notifications. Store video metadata and detection results in Amazon Timestream for temporal analysis of movement patterns.
Store all video footage in Amazon S3 and process with batch Rekognition Video.
Build custom computer vision models using SageMaker for all detection tasks.
Use Amazon Connect for security monitoring and alerting.

explanation: Kinesis Video Streams handles ingestion from 1,000 cameras. Rekognition Video stream processors provide real-time analysis without batch delay. Custom labels detect company-specific objects. EventBridge routes detection events for automated responses. SNS provides real-time alerts. Timestream stores time-series metadata for movement pattern analysis. Option B (batch S3) does not meet real-time requirements. Option C (custom models) requires ML expertise for what Rekognition provides out-of-box. Option D (Connect) is a contact center service.

stem: A company needs to implement a strategy for managing encryption keys across 200 AWS accounts. Some workloads require keys that are shared across accounts (e.g., shared S3 buckets), while others need account-specific keys. Key administrators must be separate from key users (separation of duties). How should the solutions architect implement this?

options.text: Create AWS KMS multi-Region keys in a centralized security account for shared workloads. Use KMS key policies with separate key administrator and key user principals to enforce separation of duties. Share keys with other accounts using KMS key grants or key policies with cross-account access conditions. For account-specific keys, create local KMS keys in each account using CloudFormation StackSets for consistent configuration. Use AWS Organizations SCP to prevent key deletion in workload accounts.
Create a single KMS key in the management account and share it with all 200 accounts.
Use AWS-managed keys for all encryption needs to simplify management.
Import the same key material into KMS in every account.

explanation: Multi-Region keys in a security account provide centralized management for shared workloads. KMS key policies separate administrator (create, enable, disable) from user (encrypt, decrypt) permissions. Key grants provide temporary, scoped cross-account access. Local keys in workload accounts (via StackSets) provide account-specific encryption. SCPs prevent unauthorized key deletion. Option B (single key) creates a single point of failure. Option C (AWS-managed keys) does not support cross-account sharing or custom policies. Option D (same key material everywhere) is operationally complex.

stem: A company uses Amazon API Gateway with a REST API that has 500 different endpoints. The API documentation is outdated and developers struggle to understand the API contract. The company needs to improve API documentation and enable automated client SDK generation. How should the solutions architect address this?

options.text: Export the API Gateway REST API definition as an OpenAPI (Swagger) specification. Enhance the specification with detailed descriptions, request/response models, and example payloads. Import the enhanced specification back into API Gateway to keep the API and documentation synchronized. Use API Gateway's built-in SDK generation feature to create client SDKs (JavaScript, Python, Java, Ruby, iOS, Android). Deploy the API documentation to a developer portal using the API Gateway Developer Portal from the AWS Serverless Application Repository.
Write API documentation manually in a wiki and update it when APIs change.
Generate documentation using Javadoc or similar code documentation tools.
Create a Postman collection and share it with developers.

explanation: OpenAPI specification serves as the single source of truth for API contracts, keeping documentation synchronized with the actual API. API Gateway natively supports OpenAPI import/export. Built-in SDK generation creates type-safe client libraries automatically. The Developer Portal provides self-service API discovery. Option B (wiki) quickly becomes outdated. Option C (code docs) does not document API contracts at the HTTP level. Option D (Postman) requires manual maintenance and does not generate SDKs.

stem: A company is migrating a legacy application that uses a monolithic relational database with 300 tables. The company wants to decompose the database to align with microservices boundaries, but 50 tables have complex cross-boundary foreign key relationships. How should the solutions architect handle the cross-boundary relationships during decomposition?

options.text: Replace foreign key relationships across service boundaries with eventual consistency patterns. Each microservice owns its data and publishes domain events via Amazon EventBridge when data changes. Consuming services maintain local copies of needed data (materialized views) updated through event subscriptions. For operations requiring strong consistency across services, use the saga pattern with AWS Step Functions for distributed transactions with compensating actions for failures.
Keep all 300 tables in a single shared database that all microservices access.
Create database views that span microservice boundaries to maintain relationships.
Use distributed database transactions (two-phase commit) across microservice databases.

explanation: Eventual consistency with domain events is the standard pattern for handling cross-boundary relationships in microservices. EventBridge provides reliable event delivery. Local materialized views provide fast access to needed data. Saga pattern with Step Functions handles distributed transactions with compensating logic. Option B (shared database) creates a distributed monolith. Option C (cross-boundary views) maintains coupling between services. Option D (2PC) does not scale well and creates tight coupling.

stem: A company is building a compliance-as-code platform that must validate infrastructure deployments against security policies before they are applied. The platform must check CloudFormation templates for security violations (open security groups, unencrypted storage, public S3 buckets) and block non-compliant deployments. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Implement a pre-deployment validation pipeline using AWS CloudFormation Guard to validate templates against policy rules. Integrate Guard checks into the CI/CD pipeline (CodePipeline/CodeBuild) to block deployments that violate policies. For runtime enforcement, use CloudFormation hooks that invoke Lambda functions for custom validation before resource creation. Deploy AWS Config rules as a second layer of defense to catch any non-compliant resources that bypass the pipeline.
Manually review all CloudFormation templates before deployment.
Use only AWS Config rules to detect and fix non-compliant resources after deployment.
Restrict all developers to using pre-approved CloudFormation templates only.

explanation: CloudFormation Guard provides policy-as-code validation with a declarative rule language. CI/CD integration blocks non-compliant templates before deployment. CloudFormation hooks provide runtime validation at resource creation time. Config rules provide detective controls as a safety net. This layered approach (preventive + detective) provides comprehensive compliance. Option B (manual review) does not scale. Option C (post-deployment only) allows non-compliant resources to be created. Option D (pre-approved templates) limits developer flexibility excessively.

stem: A company uses AWS PrivateLink to expose internal services across VPCs. The company has 20 internal services that need to be accessible from 50 consumer VPCs. Managing individual PrivateLink connections (20 services x 50 VPCs = 1,000 endpoints) is becoming operationally challenging. How should the solutions architect simplify this?

options.text: Deploy Amazon VPC Lattice to replace individual PrivateLink endpoints. Create a VPC Lattice service network and register all 20 internal services as VPC Lattice services. Associate all 50 consumer VPCs with the service network. VPC Lattice provides automatic service discovery, built-in load balancing, and IAM-based access control without managing individual endpoints per VPC. This reduces 1,000 endpoint connections to 50 VPC associations and 20 service registrations.
Create a shared services VPC with PrivateLink endpoints and transit all traffic through it.
Use Transit Gateway to replace PrivateLink for all service connectivity.
Consolidate all 20 services into a single PrivateLink endpoint service.

explanation: VPC Lattice simplifies service-to-service connectivity by replacing 1,000 individual endpoints with a service network model. Services register once, VPCs associate once, and VPC Lattice handles discovery, routing, and load balancing. IAM policies provide fine-grained access control. This dramatically reduces operational overhead. Option B (shared VPC proxy) creates a bottleneck and single point of failure. Option C (Transit Gateway) provides network connectivity but not service-level features. Option D (single endpoint) loses service granularity.

stem: A company's development teams deploy applications across 5 AWS Regions. Each team manages their own CloudFormation stacks independently, leading to configuration drift between Regions. Production incidents frequently occur because a configuration change applied in one Region is not applied in others. How should the solutions architect ensure consistent deployments across Regions?

options.text: Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions to deploy and manage stacks across all 5 Regions from a single template. Configure StackSets with automatic deployment to ensure new accounts in the organization automatically receive the stacks. Enable drift detection on StackSets to identify configuration differences. Use AWS CodePipeline with a multi-Region deployment action to deploy StackSet updates through a CI/CD pipeline with approval gates.
Create a wiki documenting all configuration changes and ask teams to apply them manually in each Region.
Deploy CloudFormation stacks in each Region independently from separate templates.
Use a single Region and replicate data to other Regions using S3 cross-Region replication.

explanation: StackSets ensure consistent deployment across all 5 Regions from a single template, eliminating configuration drift. Service-managed permissions integrate with Organizations. Automatic deployment ensures new accounts get the stacks. Drift detection identifies unauthorized changes. CodePipeline provides automated, approved deployment workflows. Option B (manual wiki) is error-prone. Option C (independent templates) is the current problem. Option D (single Region) does not address multi-Region deployment needs.

stem: A company is migrating a real-time data streaming application from Apache Kafka running on-premises to AWS. The application has 200 Kafka topics, 500 partitions, and processes 1 GB/sec of data. Consumer applications use Kafka consumer groups and are written in Java using the Kafka client library. The company wants a fully managed solution with minimal code changes. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Migrate to Amazon MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka). MSK provides fully managed Kafka brokers compatible with existing Kafka APIs and tools. Existing Java producer and consumer applications can connect to MSK with only a broker endpoint configuration change. Use MSK Connect for managed connectors. Configure MSK with tiered storage to automatically move older data to cost-effective storage. Use MSK Serverless for topics with variable throughput.
Migrate to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and rewrite all consumers using the Kinesis Client Library.
Deploy Apache Kafka on Amazon EC2 instances and manage it manually.
Use Amazon SQS as a replacement for all Kafka topics.

explanation: MSK provides fully managed Apache Kafka that is wire-compatible with existing Kafka clients. Existing Java applications need only a broker endpoint change. MSK manages brokers, ZooKeeper, and storage. MSK Connect provides managed connector deployment. Tiered storage reduces costs for retained data. MSK Serverless auto-scales for variable workloads. Option B (Kinesis) requires rewriting all consumers. Option C (EC2 Kafka) requires operational management. Option D (SQS) cannot replace Kafka's capabilities.

stem: A company is building a generative AI application that allows users to ask questions about internal company documents (policies, procedures, technical manuals). The application must use a large language model to generate accurate answers grounded in company documents, not general knowledge. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Implement Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) using Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases. Ingest company documents into a knowledge base backed by Amazon OpenSearch Serverless as the vector store. When users ask questions, Bedrock Knowledge Bases automatically retrieves relevant document chunks using semantic search, then passes them to a foundation model (Claude, Titan) as context for generating grounded answers. Use Bedrock Guardrails to filter inappropriate content and prevent hallucinations.
Fine-tune a foundation model on all company documents to embed the knowledge in the model weights.
Use Amazon Kendra to search for documents and display search results directly to users.
Build a custom LLM training pipeline using Amazon SageMaker.

explanation: RAG with Bedrock Knowledge Bases retrieves relevant document context before generating answers, ensuring responses are grounded in actual company documents. OpenSearch Serverless provides managed vector search for semantic retrieval. Bedrock Guardrails prevent hallucinations and filter inappropriate content. Option B (fine-tuning) is expensive, requires retraining when documents change, and may still hallucinate. Option C (Kendra search) does not generate synthesized answers. Option D (custom LLM) is extremely expensive and complex.

stem: A company is expanding to a new geographic region and must comply with data residency requirements that mandate all customer data stays within the country. The company uses AWS services that may process data in Regions outside the country. How should the solutions architect ensure data residency compliance?

options.text: Deploy all workloads in an AWS Region within the target country. Use AWS Organizations SCPs to deny all API calls that specify Regions outside the country for workload accounts in that geography. Configure S3 bucket policies with aws:RequestedRegion conditions to prevent cross-Region data transfers. Use VPC endpoints for all AWS service access to keep traffic within the AWS network. Monitor compliance using AWS Config rules that check for resources created in unauthorized Regions.
Use AWS CloudFront with geographic restrictions to control where data is accessed from.
Encrypt all data with a KMS key in the target country's Region.
Sign a custom agreement with AWS to guarantee data never leaves the country.

explanation: Region-restricting SCPs prevent any service usage in unauthorized Regions at the organization level. S3 bucket policies with Region conditions prevent cross-Region transfers. VPC endpoints keep traffic on the AWS backbone. Config rules provide detective controls for unauthorized Region usage. Together these controls enforce data residency comprehensively. Option B (CloudFront geo-restriction) controls user access locations, not data storage locations. Option C (encryption) protects data but does not control its location. Option D (custom agreement) does not provide technical controls.

stem: A company uses AWS Fargate for running containerized microservices. The operations team notices that container images in Amazon ECR are growing in size over time, with old, untagged images consuming 5 TB of storage. The team wants to automate image lifecycle management. How should the solutions architect implement this?

options.text: Configure Amazon ECR lifecycle policies on each repository. Create rules that expire untagged images older than 7 days, keep only the 10 most recent tagged images, and delete images matching specific tag prefixes (e.g., dev-*) older than 30 days. Lifecycle policies run automatically and delete images in the background. For critical production images, use ECR image tag immutability to prevent overwriting.
Write a Lambda function that deletes old images on a daily schedule.
Manually delete old images through the AWS Console monthly.
Move old images to S3 for long-term storage.

explanation: ECR lifecycle policies provide native, automatic image cleanup without custom code. Rules can target untagged images, old images by count or age, and specific tag patterns. Tag immutability prevents production image overwriting. This is the simplest and most reliable approach. Option B (Lambda cleanup) requires custom code development and maintenance. Option C (manual cleanup) does not scale. Option D (S3 archival) adds unnecessary complexity since old container images are rarely needed.

stem: A company needs to build an automated underwriting system for insurance applications. The system must analyze applicant data from multiple sources (credit reports, driving records, medical history), apply complex business rules, and generate risk scores. The rules change frequently based on regulatory requirements. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Implement the business rules using AWS Step Functions for workflow orchestration. Store and manage frequently changing business rules in AWS AppConfig with feature flags for rule versioning and gradual rollout. Use Lambda functions for each rule evaluation step (credit scoring, driving risk, medical risk). Store applicant data in DynamoDB with encryption. Use Amazon SageMaker for ML-based risk scoring models that complement rule-based evaluations. Aggregate results in Step Functions and write final decisions to DynamoDB.
Hard-code all business rules in Lambda function source code.
Store business rules in a relational database and query them during processing.
Use a commercial rules engine deployed on EC2 instances.

explanation: Step Functions orchestrates the multi-step evaluation workflow. AppConfig with feature flags enables non-deployment rule changes with gradual rollout and instant rollback. Lambda functions provide scalable, isolated rule evaluation. SageMaker adds ML-based risk assessment. DynamoDB provides fast, encrypted data access. Option B (hard-coded rules) requires deployment for every rule change. Option C (database rules) adds latency and complexity. Option D (commercial rules engine) adds licensing costs and infrastructure management.

stem: A company is migrating a legacy application that uses SOAP-based web services. The company wants to modernize the API layer to REST while maintaining backward compatibility for existing SOAP clients during the transition period. Which approach should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Deploy Amazon API Gateway as the unified API front door. Create REST API endpoints in API Gateway for new consumers. Implement a SOAP-to-REST translation layer using Lambda functions that receive SOAP XML requests, parse them, call the underlying REST service, and format the response back to SOAP XML. Use API Gateway request/response mapping templates (VTL) for simple transformations. Existing SOAP clients connect through the translation layer while new clients use REST directly.
Keep SOAP services running indefinitely alongside new REST services.
Force all clients to switch to REST immediately.
Use an ESB (Enterprise Service Bus) deployed on EC2 for protocol translation.

explanation: API Gateway provides a unified entry point for both REST and SOAP clients. Lambda-based translation layer converts between SOAP and REST formats transparently. VTL mapping templates handle simple transformations without Lambda. This allows gradual client migration from SOAP to REST. Option B (dual services indefinitely) doubles maintenance. Option C (forced migration) breaks existing integrations. Option D (ESB on EC2) adds infrastructure management overhead.

stem: A company operates a global SaaS application and must comply with GDPR requirements. When a customer exercises their right to be forgotten, all personal data must be deleted across all systems within 30 days. Data is spread across Amazon S3, DynamoDB, Aurora, ElastiCache, and CloudWatch Logs. Which approach should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Implement a data subject deletion pipeline orchestrated by AWS Step Functions. When a deletion request is received, Step Functions coordinates Lambda functions that: delete user records from DynamoDB, delete user data from Aurora, delete user objects from S3 using object key patterns, invalidate user sessions in ElastiCache, and create CloudWatch Logs deletion filters. Track deletion progress in a DynamoDB audit table. Use Amazon Macie to scan S3 for any remaining PII after deletion. Implement crypto-shredding for encrypted data by deleting the KMS key associated with the user's data.
Manually search for and delete user data from each system when requested.
Delete the user's account and assume all related data is automatically removed.
Anonymize user data instead of deleting it to maintain data integrity.

explanation: Step Functions orchestrates the multi-system deletion workflow ensuring completeness. Lambda functions handle service-specific deletion logic. The audit table provides evidence of deletion compliance. Macie verifies no PII remains. Crypto-shredding provides an efficient mechanism for encrypted data in S3. Option B (manual deletion) does not scale and risks missing data. Option C (account deletion) does not remove data from all systems. Option D (anonymization) may not satisfy GDPR's right to erasure depending on implementation.

stem: A company's application uses Amazon SQS with Lambda consumers. Messages occasionally get stuck in the dead-letter queue (DLQ) and are never reprocessed. The operations team manually investigates DLQ messages weekly, but by that time the context for failures is lost. How should the solutions architect improve DLQ handling?

options.text: Configure Amazon SQS DLQ redrive to allow reprocessing DLQ messages back to the source queue after the underlying issue is resolved. Implement CloudWatch alarms on the DLQ ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible metric to trigger immediate SNS notifications when messages arrive in the DLQ. Create a Lambda function triggered by DLQ messages that logs the failure context (message body, error details, timestamp, source queue) to CloudWatch Logs and creates an incident in the operations ticketing system via EventBridge.
Increase the maxReceiveCount on the source queue to prevent messages from going to the DLQ.
Delete the DLQ and let Lambda retries handle all failures.
Process DLQ messages with a separate Lambda function that automatically retries without investigation.

explanation: DLQ redrive enables simple reprocessing after fixes. CloudWatch alarms provide immediate notification instead of weekly manual checks. Lambda-triggered logging captures failure context when it is fresh. Automated ticketing ensures failures are tracked and investigated promptly. Option B (higher maxReceiveCount) delays but does not solve the underlying processing failure. Option C (no DLQ) loses failed messages permanently. Option D (blind retry) reprocesses without understanding or fixing the root cause.

stem: A company is building a multi-player collaborative document editing platform similar to Google Docs. The platform must support real-time collaborative editing with conflict resolution, offline editing with sync, and document version history. Which TWO components should the solutions architect include? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Use AWS AppSync with DynamoDB as the data store. AppSync's real-time subscriptions push document changes to all connected clients instantly. Use DynamoDB Conditional Writes for optimistic concurrency control to handle simultaneous edits. Implement conflict resolution using AppSync's built-in Lambda conflict handler for server-side merge logic.

Use Amazon Cognito Sync for offline data synchronization. Cognito Sync stores document edits locally when offline and automatically synchronizes changes when the device reconnects. Use Cognito Sync push notifications to alert other clients of document changes.
Use Amazon SQS to queue all document edits for sequential processing.
Store documents in Amazon S3 and use CloudFront for real-time delivery.
Use Amazon ElastiCache Pub/Sub for real-time update notifications.

explanation: AppSync (Option A) provides managed GraphQL with real-time subscriptions for pushing changes to clients, conflict resolution for simultaneous edits, and DynamoDB integration for scalable data storage. Cognito Sync (Option B) provides client-side data caching for offline editing with automatic synchronization when connectivity is restored. Together they provide real-time collaboration and offline support. Option C (SQS sequential) adds latency and does not support real-time. Option D (S3/CloudFront) is not designed for real-time collaborative editing. Option E (ElastiCache Pub/Sub) requires managing infrastructure.

stem: A company needs to implement a centralized network monitoring solution across 200 VPCs in their AWS Organization. The security team requires visibility into all network traffic patterns, the ability to detect anomalies, and historical traffic analysis for forensic investigations. Which solution should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Enable VPC Flow Logs (v5) for all VPCs and subnets, sending logs to a centralized S3 bucket in a log archive account. Use Amazon Athena with partitioned tables to query flow logs for forensic analysis. Deploy Amazon Detective for automated security investigation using graph analysis of flow log data. Use Amazon GuardDuty's VPC Flow Log analysis for real-time anomaly detection. Create CloudWatch Contributor Insights rules to identify top traffic contributors.
Deploy network monitoring agents on every EC2 instance across all VPCs.
Use AWS CloudTrail as the sole source for network monitoring.
Enable packet capture on all ENIs using tcpdump for detailed traffic analysis.

explanation: VPC Flow Logs v5 capture comprehensive traffic metadata (source, destination, ports, bytes, packets, actions). Centralized S3 storage enables cross-VPC analysis. Athena provides serverless, ad-hoc forensic queries. Detective provides automated security investigation with graph analysis. GuardDuty provides ML-based anomaly detection on flow logs. Contributor Insights identifies traffic patterns. Option B (agents) requires management on every instance. Option C (CloudTrail) captures API calls, not network traffic. Option D (tcpdump) is impractical at scale.

stem: A company is modernizing a legacy application that uses file-based integration. Partner systems deposit CSV files on an SFTP server, the application processes them sequentially, and results are deposited back. The company wants to modernize to an event-driven, parallel processing architecture. Which approach should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use AWS Transfer Family for SFTP to receive partner files directly into Amazon S3. Configure S3 event notifications to trigger an AWS Step Functions workflow for each file. The workflow uses Lambda functions to parse CSV files, validate data, and process records in parallel using Step Functions Map state. Write results back to S3 and use Transfer Family to make results available via SFTP to partners. Use DynamoDB to track file processing status and SQS dead-letter queues for failed records.
Deploy an SFTP server on EC2 and process files with a cron job.
Use Amazon AppFlow to import CSV files from partner SFTP servers.
Replace SFTP with API Gateway REST APIs for partner file submission.

explanation: Transfer Family provides managed SFTP compatible with existing partner integrations (no partner changes). S3 events trigger immediate, event-driven processing. Step Functions Map state enables parallel record processing. Lambda handles parsing and business logic. S3 + Transfer Family provides results back via SFTP. DynamoDB tracks status. DLQs capture failures. Option B (EC2 cron) replicates the legacy pattern. Option C (AppFlow) is for SaaS integrations, not SFTP. Option D (API replacement) requires all partners to change their integration.

stem: A company runs an application on Amazon ECS that experiences memory leaks over time. Containers gradually consume more memory until they crash with OOM (Out of Memory) errors, causing brief service disruptions. Restarting containers temporarily fixes the issue. How should the solutions architect mitigate the impact while the development team fixes the root cause?

options.text: Configure ECS container health checks that monitor memory utilization. Set ECS task definition memory hard limits to prevent OOM kills from affecting the node. Configure the ECS service with deployment configuration minimumHealthyPercent of 100% and maximumPercent of 200% to ensure new tasks start before unhealthy ones are stopped. Implement a CloudWatch alarm on container memory utilization that triggers an ECS service force-new-deployment via Lambda when memory exceeds 80%, proactively recycling containers before they crash.
Increase the container memory allocation to delay the OOM crash.
Reduce the number of running tasks to free up memory on nodes.
Restart all containers on a fixed daily schedule regardless of memory usage.

explanation: Proactive container recycling before OOM prevents service disruptions. Health checks detect degraded containers. Memory hard limits prevent node-level impact. Deployment configuration ensures replacement tasks start before old ones stop. CloudWatch alarm triggers automated recycling when memory reaches 80%, well before the crash. Option B (more memory) delays but does not solve the problem. Option C (fewer tasks) reduces capacity. Option D (daily restart) is too infrequent if leaks happen faster and disrupts all containers simultaneously.

stem: A company is building a platform for processing and analyzing genomic data. Each genome dataset is 200 GB. The platform must align reads, call variants, and run statistical analyses. Processing a single genome takes 8 hours on a 96-vCPU machine. The company processes 100 genomes per week. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use AWS Batch with Spot Instances for compute-intensive genomic processing. Configure Batch job definitions with 96-vCPU EC2 instances (r6i.24xlarge or similar) for alignment and variant calling. Use Amazon S3 for storing genome datasets and results. Deploy FSx for Lustre as a high-throughput scratch file system linked to S3 for fast data access during processing. Use AWS Step Functions to orchestrate the multi-step genomic pipeline with automatic retry for Spot interruptions.
Use AWS Lambda for genome processing with maximum memory configuration.
Deploy a permanent cluster of 100 EC2 instances for genome processing.
Use Amazon EMR with Apache Spark for all genomic analysis.

explanation: AWS Batch manages job scheduling and Spot Instance procurement for cost optimization. 96-vCPU instances match the processing requirements. FSx for Lustre provides the high-throughput file system needed for genomic I/O. S3 provides durable storage for datasets and results. Step Functions orchestrates the multi-step pipeline. Spot with retry handles interruptions. Option B (Lambda) is limited to 10 GB memory and 15-minute timeout. Option C (permanent cluster) wastes resources when not processing. Option D (EMR Spark) is not optimized for single-genome, single-machine processing.

stem: A company needs to implement a tagging strategy across their AWS Organization that ensures all resources are tagged with mandatory tags (Owner, CostCenter, Environment, Application). Resources without these tags should be prevented from being created. How should the solutions architect enforce this?

options.text: Create AWS Organizations tag policies that define the mandatory tag keys and their allowed values. Deploy SCPs that deny resource creation actions (ec2:RunInstances, rds:CreateDBInstance, s3:CreateBucket, etc.) when the required tags are not present in the request using the aws:RequestTag condition key. Create AWS Config rules (required-tags) to detect existing untagged resources and trigger SSM Automation remediation to notify resource owners. Use AWS Cost Explorer with cost allocation tags to tie costs to business units.
Create IAM policies in each account that deny resource creation without tags.
Use AWS Config alone to detect and delete untagged resources.
Send monthly reports to teams listing their untagged resources.

explanation: Tag policies define mandatory tags and allowed values at the organization level. SCPs with aws:RequestTag conditions prevent resource creation without required tags (preventive control). Config rules detect existing untagged resources (detective control). SSM Automation notifies owners for remediation. Cost allocation tags enable cost tracking. Option B (IAM policies) can be overridden by account admins. Option C (Config delete) is destructive and reactive. Option D (monthly reports) relies on voluntary compliance.

stem: A company runs a PostgreSQL database on Amazon RDS with 500 GB of data. The company needs to provide developers with copies of the production database for testing, but creating full copies takes 2 hours and costs $75 per copy in storage. Developers need 10 database copies simultaneously. How should the solutions architect reduce the time and cost of providing test databases?

options.text: Use Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with the Aurora clone feature. Aurora clones create a copy of the database in minutes (not hours) using copy-on-write storage, meaning clones share the original storage pages and only consume additional storage for changed pages. This reduces both clone creation time to minutes and storage cost to only the delta. Developers can create and delete clones independently without affecting the production database.
Create 10 RDS read replicas and let developers use them for testing.
Take an RDS snapshot and restore it 10 times for each developer.
Use pg_dump to export the database and import it into 10 separate RDS instances.

explanation: Aurora clones use copy-on-write storage, creating database copies in minutes instead of hours. Clones initially consume zero additional storage, only growing as developers make changes. This dramatically reduces both time and cost for 10 simultaneous copies. Option B (read replicas) are read-only and share the production workload. Option C (snapshot restore x10) takes 2 hours per restore and consumes full storage per copy ($750 total). Option D (pg_dump x10) is even slower and requires full storage.

stem: A company is modernizing its notification system. The legacy system sends emails, SMS, and push notifications through separate code paths with different retry logic and template engines. The company wants a unified notification service on AWS. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon Simple Email Service (SES) for email delivery with email templates. Use Amazon SNS for SMS delivery and mobile push notifications to iOS/Android devices. Create a unified notification microservice on Lambda behind API Gateway that accepts notification requests and routes them to the appropriate delivery channel (SES/SNS). Store notification templates in DynamoDB with support for personalization variables. Use Amazon Pinpoint for user segmentation and campaign management. Track delivery status using SES/SNS delivery callbacks to a Lambda function that updates notification status in DynamoDB.
Use Amazon SNS for all notification types including email.
Deploy a self-managed mail server on EC2 for email notifications.
Use third-party notification APIs for all channels.

explanation: SES provides high-deliverability email with templates. SNS provides SMS and mobile push with native iOS/Android support. A unified Lambda microservice abstracts channel routing from callers. DynamoDB stores templates with personalization. Pinpoint adds user segmentation for targeted notifications. Delivery callbacks provide status tracking. Option B (SNS for email) has limited email features. Option C (self-managed mail) requires infrastructure management and IP reputation management. Option D (third-party) adds dependency and cost.

stem: A company needs to build a system for detecting and responding to distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks on their web application. The application uses Amazon CloudFront, Application Load Balancer, and Amazon EC2. The company wants automatic mitigation with no manual intervention. Which architecture should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Enable AWS Shield Advanced on all internet-facing resources (CloudFront, ALB, Elastic IPs). Shield Advanced provides automatic DDoS detection and mitigation for Layer 3, 4, and 7 attacks. Deploy AWS WAF with rate-based rules on CloudFront and ALB to automatically block IP addresses exceeding request thresholds. Enable Shield Advanced automatic application layer DDoS mitigation, which automatically creates WAF rules to respond to detected Layer 7 attacks. Configure Shield Advanced health-based detection using Route 53 health checks for faster detection.
Over-provision EC2 instances to absorb DDoS traffic.
Use AWS Network Firewall to block all suspicious traffic.
Configure CloudFront geographic restrictions to block traffic from suspicious countries.

explanation: Shield Advanced provides comprehensive DDoS protection with automatic detection and mitigation at Layers 3, 4, and 7. WAF rate-based rules automatically block high-volume IP addresses. Automatic application layer mitigation creates WAF rules in response to detected attacks without manual intervention. Health-based detection provides faster response. Option B (over-provisioning) is expensive and does not mitigate the attack. Option C (Network Firewall) does not provide DDoS-specific detection. Option D (geo-blocking) blocks legitimate users and does not stop distributed attacks.

stem: A company uses AWS CloudTrail across 300 accounts in their AWS Organization. The company needs to detect when IAM policies are modified in production accounts and automatically revert unauthorized changes. Which solution should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Create an EventBridge rule in the management account that matches CloudTrail events for IAM policy modifications (PutRolePolicy, AttachRolePolicy, CreatePolicy, etc.) in production account OUs. Route matching events to a Lambda function that checks if the change was made by an authorized principal (comparing against an allow-list stored in DynamoDB). If unauthorized, the Lambda function automatically reverts the IAM policy change to its previous state using the IAM API and sends an alert via SNS. Store all policy change events in DynamoDB for audit trail.
Review CloudTrail logs manually every day for IAM policy changes.
Use AWS Config rules to detect non-compliant IAM policies weekly.
Prevent all IAM policy changes in production using SCPs.

explanation: EventBridge rules on CloudTrail events provide real-time detection of IAM changes. Lambda-based authorization checking against an allow-list enables automated decision making. Automatic reversion restores the previous policy state. SNS alerts notify the security team. DynamoDB audit trail provides compliance evidence. Option B (manual review) is delayed and does not scale. Option C (weekly Config) is too slow for security-critical changes. Option D (blanket SCP deny) prevents all legitimate IAM changes too.

stem: A company's web application uses Amazon CloudFront with an ALB origin. The company notices that about 15% of traffic hitting CloudFront is from web scrapers and bots that consume resources without generating revenue. The company wants to manage bot traffic without blocking legitimate search engine crawlers. How should the solutions architect address this?

options.text: Deploy AWS WAF with the Bot Control managed rule group on the CloudFront distribution. Configure Bot Control to allow verified bots (Googlebot, Bingbot) while blocking or challenging unverified bots and scrapers. Use the targeted inspection level for advanced bot detection using browser fingerprinting and behavior analysis. Create custom WAF rules to rate-limit specific bot patterns. Monitor bot traffic using WAF dashboard and logs to S3 for analysis.
Block all user agents that identify as bots using a custom WAF rule.
Use robots.txt to prevent bots from accessing the application.
Add CAPTCHA to every page of the application.

explanation: WAF Bot Control distinguishes between verified bots (legitimate crawlers with IP verification) and unverified bots/scrapers. Targeted inspection uses advanced techniques (browser fingerprinting, mouse movements, JS challenges) to detect sophisticated bots. Custom rules handle specific patterns. Allowing verified bots maintains SEO. Option B (block all bot UAs) blocks legitimate crawlers, hurting SEO. Option C (robots.txt) is advisory and ignored by malicious bots. Option D (universal CAPTCHA) degrades user experience for all visitors.

stem: A company is modernizing a legacy system that processes insurance claims. The system currently uses a human workflow where claims adjusters manually review documents, verify coverage, and approve or deny claims. The process takes an average of 5 days per claim. The company wants to automate as much as possible while keeping humans in the loop for complex decisions. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use AWS Step Functions for the overall claims workflow orchestration. Implement Amazon Textract for document extraction, Amazon Comprehend for text classification, and Lambda functions for automated coverage verification against policy data in DynamoDB. For complex cases requiring human review, integrate Amazon A2I (Augmented AI) with a private workforce of claims adjusters. A2I routes complex claims to human reviewers with a customizable review UI. Once reviewed, the workflow continues automatically. Track all decisions in DynamoDB for audit.
Build a fully automated system with no human review capability.
Keep the current manual process and digitize the paper documents.
Use Amazon Mechanical Turk for all claims review.

explanation: Step Functions orchestrates the end-to-end workflow. Textract extracts document data. Comprehend classifies claims. Lambda automates rule-based decisions. A2I provides human-in-the-loop review for complex cases with a private, trusted workforce. The combination automates routine claims while ensuring expert review for complex ones, reducing processing time from days to hours. Option B (no human review) risks errors on complex claims. Option C (digitize only) does not automate processing. Option D (Mechanical Turk) uses public workers, inappropriate for sensitive insurance data.

stem: A company is building a real-time fraud detection system for credit card transactions. The system must evaluate each transaction within 50 milliseconds and make an approve/decline decision based on transaction patterns, user behavior, and known fraud indicators. The system processes 10,000 transactions per second at peak. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Deploy Amazon SageMaker real-time inference endpoints with auto-scaling for the fraud detection ML model. Front the endpoints with Amazon API Gateway for transaction submission. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to store user behavioral profiles and transaction history for low-latency feature lookups (required for the 50ms budget). Pre-compute fraud indicators using Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics and cache results in Redis. Use Amazon DynamoDB for persistent transaction storage.
Use AWS Lambda for fraud detection with a model loaded from S3 on each invocation.
Process transactions in batch with Amazon EMR running Spark ML every hour.
Store all transactions in Amazon Redshift and run SQL-based fraud detection queries.

explanation: SageMaker real-time endpoints provide consistent sub-50ms ML inference with auto-scaling for 10K TPS. ElastiCache Redis provides microsecond feature lookups essential for the tight latency budget. Kinesis Data Analytics pre-computes streaming fraud indicators. API Gateway provides the transaction submission interface. DynamoDB stores transactions persistently. Option B (Lambda with S3 model loading) has cold start and model loading overhead. Option C (batch EMR) is not real-time. Option D (Redshift SQL) cannot achieve 50ms per-transaction latency.

stem: A company's AWS environment has grown organically, resulting in inconsistent naming conventions, tag structures, and resource configurations across 150 accounts. The company wants to establish and enforce standards going forward without disrupting existing workloads. Which approach should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Create AWS Service Catalog portfolios with standardized product templates (EC2, RDS, S3, VPC) that enforce naming conventions, required tags, and security configurations. Deploy SCPs that gradually restrict direct resource creation, requiring resources to be provisioned through Service Catalog. Use AWS Config conformance packs to identify non-compliant existing resources. Create a remediation roadmap using Config findings, prioritizing security-critical resources. Implement CloudFormation Guard for validating templates in CI/CD pipelines.
Delete all non-compliant resources immediately and recreate them with proper standards.
Document standards in a wiki and ask teams to follow them voluntarily.
Assign one person to review every resource creation request manually.

explanation: Service Catalog provides self-service resource provisioning with built-in standards. Gradual SCP enforcement avoids disrupting existing workloads. Config conformance packs identify existing non-compliance for prioritized remediation. CloudFormation Guard validates templates before deployment. This approach enforces standards going forward while providing a path to remediate existing resources. Option B (delete all) disrupts existing workloads. Option C (wiki) does not enforce standards. Option D (manual review) does not scale.

stem: A company runs an Amazon Aurora MySQL database with 2 TB of data. The operations team needs to restore the database to a specific point in time 3 hours ago due to an application bug that corrupted data. However, they need to verify the restored data before switching production traffic. How should the solutions architect perform this recovery?

options.text: Use Aurora's point-in-time recovery (PITR) feature to restore the database to a new Aurora cluster at the specific timestamp 3 hours ago. Aurora maintains continuous backups with 1-second granularity. The restored cluster is independent and can be verified without affecting the production cluster. After verification, update the application's database endpoint to point to the restored cluster. Alternatively, use Aurora Backtrack to rewind the existing cluster to the desired point in time (if enabled), which is faster but affects the production cluster directly.
Restore from the most recent automated snapshot, which may be up to 24 hours old.
Replay all transaction logs from the binary log manually.
Use DMS to copy data from a point-in-time backup to the production database.

explanation: Aurora PITR restores to a new cluster at any second within the backup retention period, enabling verification before cutover. The 1-second granularity ensures precise recovery to just before the corruption. The new cluster allows independent verification. Aurora Backtrack (if pre-enabled) provides in-place rewind which is faster but affects the running cluster. Option B (snapshot) may lose hours of valid data. Option C (manual log replay) is complex and error-prone. Option D (DMS) adds unnecessary complexity.

stem: A company is migrating an application that uses a commercial load balancer with advanced traffic management features including URL rewriting, header manipulation, weighted routing, and A/B testing. Which AWS service provides equivalent capabilities?

options.text: Use an Application Load Balancer (ALB) with advanced routing rules. Configure listener rules with path-based and host-based routing. Use ALB fixed response actions, redirect actions, and forward actions with multiple target groups using weighted routing for A/B testing. For URL rewriting and header manipulation, use ALB listener rule conditions and actions, or deploy Lambda@Edge/CloudFront Functions for complex transformations. Use AWS WAF integration for security filtering.
Use a Network Load Balancer with TCP-level routing.
Use Amazon API Gateway for all traffic management.
Deploy HAProxy on EC2 instances for load balancing.

explanation: ALB provides Layer 7 routing with path-based and host-based rules, weighted target groups for A/B testing, redirect/fixed-response actions, and WAF integration. Lambda@Edge handles complex URL rewriting and header manipulation. Weighted routing enables gradual traffic shifting. Option B (NLB) operates at Layer 4 without HTTP-level features. Option C (API Gateway) is for API management, not general load balancing. Option D (HAProxy) requires infrastructure management.

stem: A company needs to implement end-to-end encryption for data in transit between microservices running on Amazon ECS. The encryption must use mutual TLS (mTLS) where both the client and server authenticate each other using certificates. Certificate management must be automated. Which solution should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Deploy AWS App Mesh as the service mesh for ECS services. Configure App Mesh to enforce mTLS between all services using certificates issued by AWS Certificate Manager Private CA (ACM PCA). App Mesh Envoy proxies handle TLS termination and origination automatically. ACM PCA provides automated certificate issuance and rotation. Configure App Mesh TLS policy to require client certificate validation for all virtual services.
Implement application-level TLS using self-signed certificates stored in Secrets Manager.
Use ALB with HTTPS listeners between all services.
Deploy VPN connections between all ECS tasks for encryption.

explanation: App Mesh provides transparent mTLS between services through Envoy sidecar proxies. ACM PCA automates certificate issuance and rotation, eliminating manual certificate management. TLS policies enforce mutual authentication. Applications do not need to handle TLS (Envoy handles it). Option B (self-signed certs) requires manual certificate management and application code changes. Option C (ALB HTTPS) provides server authentication but not mutual authentication. Option D (VPN) is impractical between containers.

stem: A company needs to ensure that all AWS API calls from their 200-account organization go through a centralized egress point for API call monitoring and control. Some accounts should be restricted from calling certain AWS APIs (e.g., Lambda in sandbox accounts). Which solution should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Use AWS Organizations Service Control Policies (SCPs) to restrict which AWS API calls each account or OU can make. For example, create an SCP that denies lambda:* actions in sandbox account OUs. Use CloudTrail organization trail to centrally log all API calls across all 200 accounts. Create EventBridge rules to detect and alert on unauthorized API call attempts. Use AWS Config organization rules to verify that restricted services are not being used in restricted accounts.
Route all AWS API calls through a proxy server for monitoring.
Use IAM permission boundaries in each account to restrict API calls.
Deploy VPC endpoints in each account and block internet access to AWS APIs.

explanation: SCPs provide organization-level API restrictions that cannot be overridden by account administrators. CloudTrail organization trail logs all API calls centrally. EventBridge detects unauthorized attempts in real-time. Config rules verify ongoing compliance. This is the native, scalable approach for API governance across organizations. Option B (proxy server) cannot intercept AWS API calls made using IAM credentials. Option C (permission boundaries) can be modified by account admins. Option D (VPC endpoints) only affect API calls from within VPCs, not console or CLI calls.

stem: A company's application writes data to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. The producer application frequently encounters ProvisionedThroughputExceededException because traffic is unevenly distributed across shards. Some shards receive 5x more traffic than others. How should the solutions architect resolve this?

options.text: Implement a partition key strategy that distributes data evenly across shards. Replace the current sequential or low-cardinality partition key with a high-cardinality key (e.g., UUID or hash of multiple fields). If the natural partition key has hot spots, append a random suffix to distribute records across shards while maintaining order within logical groups using enhanced fan-out consumers. Monitor per-shard metrics using CloudWatch's IncomingBytes and IncomingRecords metrics to verify even distribution.
Double the number of shards to increase overall stream capacity.
Enable Kinesis Data Streams on-demand mode to automatically scale shards.
Reduce the number of producers writing to the stream.

explanation: Uneven shard distribution is caused by partition key hot spots. High-cardinality partition keys ensure even distribution across shards. Random suffixes distribute hot keys while enhanced fan-out maintains per-consumer ordering. CloudWatch per-shard metrics verify distribution. Option B (more shards) increases capacity but does not fix the hot shard problem if keys are still unevenly distributed. Option C (on-demand) adapts capacity but individual shard limits remain. Option D (fewer producers) reduces throughput without fixing distribution.

stem: A company needs to build a data pipeline that transforms semi-structured JSON data from IoT devices into a structured format for analytics. The JSON schema varies across device types and changes frequently as new device firmware is deployed. The pipeline must handle schema evolution gracefully without data loss. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Ingest IoT data into Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Use Firehose's data transformation feature with a Lambda function to normalize JSON structures. Store raw data in an S3 raw zone (preserving original data regardless of schema). Use AWS Glue Schema Registry to manage schema versions and enforce compatibility rules. Use AWS Glue crawlers to discover new schemas automatically and update the Glue Data Catalog. Use Glue ETL jobs with schema evolution support to transform data into Parquet format in a curated S3 zone.
Define a fixed schema and reject any data that does not conform.
Store all data as unstructured text files without any schema management.
Use Amazon RDS with ALTER TABLE to add new columns for each schema change.

explanation: Preserving raw data in S3 ensures no data loss regardless of schema changes. Glue Schema Registry manages schema versions with compatibility checking. Glue crawlers automatically discover new schemas. Glue ETL with schema evolution handles new fields gracefully. Firehose with Lambda normalization handles device-specific variations. This approach accommodates frequent schema changes. Option B (fixed schema) rejects valid data. Option C (no schema) makes analytics difficult. Option D (RDS ALTER TABLE) requires downtime and does not scale for IoT.

stem: A company is migrating a legacy application with 80 TB of data in an on-premises SAN (Storage Area Network). The SAN provides block storage to multiple application servers simultaneously via iSCSI. The company needs an AWS storage solution that supports multi-attach block storage for their migrated EC2 instances. Which solution should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon EBS io2 Block Express volumes with Multi-Attach enabled. Multi-Attach allows a single io2 volume to be attached to up to 16 EC2 instances in the same Availability Zone simultaneously. The application must manage concurrent access using a cluster-aware file system (like GFS2 or OCFS2) to prevent data corruption. For data migration, use AWS DataSync to transfer the 80 TB from the on-premises SAN to an interim EBS volume.
Use Amazon EFS for block storage needs since it supports multi-instance access.
Use Amazon S3 as a block storage replacement with S3 API access.
Deploy AWS Storage Gateway in volume mode for shared block storage.

explanation: EBS io2 Multi-Attach provides shared block storage for up to 16 instances, replacing SAN iSCSI functionality. Cluster-aware file systems manage concurrent access safely. io2 Block Express provides high performance. DataSync handles the 80 TB migration. Option B (EFS) is a file system (NFS), not block storage, and has different I/O characteristics. Option C (S3) is object storage, not block storage. Option D (Storage Gateway volumes) is for hybrid scenarios and adds latency.

stem: A company needs to provide third-party auditors with limited, temporary access to specific AWS resources for compliance auditing purposes. Auditors need read-only access to CloudTrail logs, Config data, and specific S3 buckets containing compliance documentation. Access should be limited to 5 business days and fully logged. Which solution should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Create an IAM role with a read-only policy scoped to CloudTrail, Config, and specific S3 buckets. Use IAM Identity Center to create a temporary permission set with a 12-hour session duration. Provide auditors with temporary SSO credentials through IAM Identity Center. Set the permission set with a 5-day expiration by scheduling a Lambda function to remove auditor access after 5 days. Enable CloudTrail logging to capture all API calls made by auditors. Require MFA for the auditor SSO login.
Create long-term IAM users with access keys for auditors.
Give auditors access to the AWS root account for full visibility.
Export all audit data to a shared Google Drive folder.

explanation: IAM Identity Center provides SSO with temporary credentials and configurable session duration. Scoped read-only policies limit access to required resources only. Lambda-based expiration ensures access is automatically revoked after 5 days. CloudTrail captures all auditor actions for audit trail. MFA adds an extra security layer. Option B (long-term keys) creates permanent access that might not be revoked. Option C (root access) is a severe security risk. Option D (Google Drive) loses audit trail and AWS-native access controls.

stem: A company operates a multi-tenant application where tenants share Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL tables. Some tenants run expensive analytical queries that consume significant database resources, affecting performance for other tenants. The company cannot separate tenants into different databases due to cross-tenant reporting requirements. How should the solutions architect isolate tenant query impact?

options.text: Configure PostgreSQL resource management using pgbouncer for connection pooling with per-tenant connection limits. Implement PostgreSQL's pg_cron extension with statement_timeout settings per tenant role. Create separate database roles for each tenant with statement_timeout limits. Use Aurora reader instances dedicated to analytical workloads and route analytical queries there. Implement application-level query queuing that limits concurrent expensive queries per tenant.
Upgrade to the largest Aurora instance class to handle all queries.
Rate-limit all API requests equally regardless of query complexity.
Disable analytical queries entirely during business hours.

explanation: Per-tenant connection limits via pgbouncer prevent any tenant from monopolizing connections. Statement_timeout per tenant role prevents runaway queries. Reader instances isolate analytical workloads from transactional ones. Application-level queuing limits concurrent expensive queries. Together these provide multi-tenant query isolation without database separation. Option B (bigger instance) delays but does not solve the problem. Option C (equal rate limiting) does not account for query complexity. Option D (disable analytics) removes functionality.

stem: A company needs to build an automated code review system that analyzes code commits for security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to coding standards. The system must integrate with the company's existing GitHub repositories. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon CodeGuru Reviewer to automatically analyze code in GitHub repositories. CodeGuru uses ML-trained models to detect security vulnerabilities, resource leaks, race conditions, and code quality issues. Configure CodeGuru to trigger on pull requests in GitHub, providing inline comments with recommendations. Use Amazon CodeGuru Security for identifying security vulnerabilities based on OWASP and CWE. Integrate findings into AWS Security Hub for centralized security visibility.
Deploy SonarQube on EC2 instances for code analysis.
Write custom Lambda functions to parse code files for common patterns.
Rely on manual code reviews by senior developers for all changes.

explanation: CodeGuru Reviewer provides ML-powered automated code review integrated with GitHub. It detects hard-to-find bugs (resource leaks, race conditions) beyond static analysis. CodeGuru Security identifies security vulnerabilities. GitHub integration provides inline PR comments. Security Hub aggregation provides centralized visibility. Option B (SonarQube) requires infrastructure management. Option C (custom Lambda) requires building and maintaining analysis rules. Option D (manual reviews) does not scale and misses ML-detectable patterns.

stem: A company is migrating a legacy system that uses a proprietary message queue with guaranteed exactly-once delivery. The system processes financial transactions where duplicate processing would cause monetary errors. Which AWS messaging service should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon SQS FIFO queues with content-based deduplication enabled. FIFO queues guarantee exactly-once processing within the 5-minute deduplication window. Configure the message deduplication ID based on transaction IDs to prevent duplicate submissions. The application must also implement idempotent message processing (checking if a transaction ID has already been processed in DynamoDB before processing) as a belt-and-suspenders approach for transactions that may span the deduplication window.
Use Amazon SQS Standard queues with application-level deduplication.
Use Amazon SNS with message filtering for transaction processing.
Use Amazon MQ with ActiveMQ for JMS compatibility.

explanation: SQS FIFO queues provide exactly-once delivery within the 5-minute deduplication window using message deduplication IDs. Content-based deduplication uses message body hashing. For financial transactions, combining FIFO deduplication with application-level idempotency (DynamoDB transaction ID tracking) provides the strongest guarantee against duplicate processing. Option B (Standard queues) provides at-least-once delivery. Option C (SNS) is pub/sub, not a queue. Option D (Amazon MQ) provides at-least-once, not exactly-once.

stem: A company is building a platform that generates synthetic training data for machine learning models. The platform must generate realistic images, text, and tabular data that preserves statistical properties of the original data without exposing actual customer PII. Which architecture should the solutions architect recommend?

options.text: Use Amazon Bedrock with foundation models (Claude, Stable Diffusion, Titan) for generating synthetic text and images based on prompts describing desired data characteristics. For tabular data, use Amazon SageMaker with a trained Variational Autoencoder (VAE) or Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) that learns statistical distributions from the original data and generates synthetic records. Validate synthetic data quality using Amazon SageMaker Processing jobs that compare statistical properties (distributions, correlations) between original and synthetic data. Store generated data in Amazon S3 with encryption.
Copy production data and manually redact PII fields.
Use Amazon Macie to anonymize data by removing all PII automatically.
Generate random data without any relationship to original data characteristics.

explanation: Bedrock foundation models generate realistic synthetic text and images. SageMaker-trained VAE/GAN models produce tabular data that preserves statistical properties (distributions, correlations) without containing actual PII. SageMaker Processing validates synthetic data quality. This produces useful training data while protecting privacy. Option B (redaction) may still leak PII through combinations of quasi-identifiers. Option C (Macie) detects PII but does not generate synthetic replacements. Option D (random data) does not preserve statistical properties needed for effective ML training.

stem: A company operates a multi-account environment and needs to ensure that all Amazon EC2 instances across the organization are patched within 48 hours of a critical security patch release. The company has 5,000 EC2 instances across 100 accounts running both Windows and Linux. Which solution should the solutions architect implement?

options.text: Deploy AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager with organization-wide configuration using AWS Organizations integration. Create patch baselines for each OS (Windows, Amazon Linux, Ubuntu) that auto-approve critical security patches. Configure maintenance windows that automatically patch instances within 48 hours. Use SSM State Manager to ensure the SSM agent is installed and running on all instances. Deploy SSM Inventory to track patch compliance.
